picks.blurb: Iowa State Football vs. UCF Knights: 3 Bold Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Featured Stories Cyclones in the Pros The Iowa State Cyclones are riding some positive momentum into their Week 12 matchup against the UCF Knights. Last weekend, the Cyclones dominated the Cincinnati Bearcats at Jack Trice Stadium, winning 41-13. That evened their record out at 5-5 on the year, moving them one game away from becoming bowl-eligible. They will look to accomplish that feat on the road against a UCF squad that is also 5-5 on the season, with a marquee victory over the BYU Cougars when they were undefeated and the No. 2 team in the country. How will this Friday night game in Orlando turn out? Here are some bold predictions for the contest. Aiden Flora Held in Check Nov 14, 2026; Ames, Iowa, USA; Iowa State Cyclones running back Aiden Flora (21) strikes the Heisman Pose after scoring against the Cincinnati Bearcats at Jack Trice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Reese Strickland-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The leading rusher in the country, Aiden Flora, has turned into a bona fide star for Iowa State. He has been dominant during Big 12 play , but he is going to be challenged by a stout Knights run defense. The leading rusher in the country, Aiden Flora, has turned into a bona fide star for Iowa State. He has been dominant during Big 12 play , but he is going to be challenged by a stout Knights run defense. UCF has one of the top-ranked run defenses in the country, coming in at No. 20 in the nation with a run defense grade of 91.2. Finding room is going to be a challenge for a team that ranks near the bottom of the country in run blocking, with the Cyclones earning a woeful 55.1 run-blocking grade. Knowing the success Flora has had, the lack of success in the trenches for the Iowa State offensive line to open lanes is shocking. Flora is going to handle a heavy workload, but he will be held in check as his streak of 175+ yard games will come to an end. But he will still have a solid game with 125 rushing yards. Defense Continues Trending in the Right Direction The Cyclones' defense has been challenged throughout the season, with all of their Power Conference opponents being ranked in the top 80 in points per drive . That streak will continue against the Knights, but Iowa State will have answers for them. An injury to quarterback Alonza Barnett III has kept UCF from truly reaching its potential. Riding some positive momentum after holding Cincinnati to 13 points, Jesse Bobbit's unit will continue that success against the Knights, who don’t excel along the offensive line. The Knights are ranked 108th with a pass-blocking grade of 57.2 and they are 115th in run-blocking with a grade of 54.3. Iowa State isn’t elite as a run defense or pass rush, but they should have an edge in the trenches to take advantage of. The Cyclones will pick up a hard-fought win, 27-21. Jaylen Raynor will have two touchdowns, taking full advantage of the Knights’ defense, which will sell out to try to stop Flora, continuing his hot streak after a rocky start to his Iowa State tenure. The Knights are trending toward relief in the secondary, with both DJ Bell and Kahmel Johnson ruled probable in Tuesday's report. However, the unit won't be fully all-hands-on-deck, as Demari Henderson was ruled out . As for Bell, a senior, and Johnson, they are set to return to their rotational roles, barring any setbacks. Bell, after missing four games, would be back rotating with Jayden Bellamy and Antione Jackson . Johnson, after missing two games, would return as the backup nickelback behind Braeden Marshall . Three Knights were ruled questionable in Tuesday's report. Another senior that is questionable for Friday's Senior Knight game is linebacker Jayden Jennings , who, despite being on the Knights' reports for eight weeks of conference games, has always managed to play. He has only been designated questionable for one of these weeks before this one, however. So, should he miss Friday's game, Tackett Curtis and Jahleel Culbreath would be in line to take on greater roles in the Knights' linebacker rotation. Finally, after missing last weekend's game against Arizona State, Waden Charles has the chance to return after just a one-game absence. Should he be out for a second game, however, the Knights would still have several receiving threats in the form of Josh Derry , Tyren Hornes , Duane Thomas Jr. and tight end Caden Piening . WEDNESDAY UPDATE: Charles was upgraded to probable for the Knights' Wednesday report. Joining Bell and Johnson in getting designated probable are Piening and running back Duke Watson . The designation implies a likely chance for Watson, the Knights' leading rusher this season, to return after missing Saturday's game against Arizona State. However, should he suffer any setbacks, he has Taevion Swint and Landen Chambers behind him. Meanwhile, Piening managed to play last Saturday against the Sun Devils, catching four passes for 35 yards, after going into the weekend with questionable designations. home.headline: UCF Q&A: How does Lewis Carter’s return help the Knights?
home.blurb: “Lewis, like a lot of our guys, he's been out a long time,” said coach Scott Frost . “He’s going to continue to get better as he gets closer to 100% and shakes the rust off a little bit. He’s a great person and a great player. He’s one of our leaders and we’ve missed him.” Ex-UCF star Tacko Fall, now with 76ers, says time was right for NBA return Hurricanes star Malachi Toney nearing return from ankle injury Florida & Caribbean Experiences Branded Content Paid Partner Content Services About the Orlando Sentinel 🎁 Gift idea: Sentinel's 150th book This was supposed to be Lewis Carter ‘s breakout season. Instead, the UCF linebacker and team captain found himself on the sideline with an injury that cost him half the season. Carter, 22, returned against Arizona State on Saturday, playing for the first time since Sept. 19 against Georgia State. “I was flying around and had a lot of energy. It felt good,” said Carter, who finished with three tackles on 25 snaps. In Carter’s absence, transfer Tackett Curtis has emerged as the team’s leading tackler (67), along with Jahleel Culbreath (44), Jaden Jennings (23), and Cole Kozlowski (19), who returned after a court order in fall camp. Carter spent much of his time off the field mentoring his teammates. “I was being hands-on as much as I could within the meeting rooms and on the sidelines,” said Carter. “I was trying to be a voice for the guys throughout.” How important are turnovers against Iowa State? Iowa State has turned the ball over just nine times — tied for the second-fewest turnovers given up in the Big 12 this season. Meanwhile, UCF has struggled to create takeaways lately, failing to force a turnover for the second time in its last three games. The Knights are 1-9 under Frost when they don’t force a miscue, including an 0-3 mark this season. “At times, we’ve been really good and the games where we’ve gotten turnovers, we’ve won those games,” said Frost. “That’s no secret. That’s the biggest stat in football.” Frost credits the takeaways with not only giving the team much-needed momentum, but also shortening the field and giving the offense more chances to score. Something the Knights could use more of over the remaining two games. How can the Knights get more pressure on the quarterback? UCF has gone back-to-back games without sacking a quarterback for the first time since 2021. The Knights have 16 sacks heading into this week’s showdown, tied for the second-fewest in the Big 12 with Iowa State. “We’ve actually gotten a lot of pressure, but we haven’t gotten the sacks,” said Frost. “As far as affecting throws, our guys have been pretty good. We’ve just got to finish those plays. There were at least three the other night when he had free shots and didn’t get the quarterback down.” Bianchi: Six wins, zero apologies! home.blurb: Throughout the long seven weeks, including the bye, Carter said he kept his head down and attacked recovery. He made progress, and the Frost hinted at an inevitable return since Oct. 26. UCF's coach said the senior was a game-time decision before the Oct. 30 matchup against the Baylor Bears, and if not, he'd be a game-time decision on the road against the Kansas Jayhawks. Carter didn't return in either. However, Frost's optimism about his availability was a positive sign that the Knights' defense would get their captain back. Carter sustained a knee injury in Week 3 against the Georgia State Panthers, as fans and media saw him enter the medical tent. Coach Scott Frost said he was unaware his senior was injured, and it spiraled into missing the star linebacker. Their captain made his conference debut against Arizona State. He had a quiet performance, posting three solo tackles. The star linebacker said he's 100% and wants to put his best foot forward to help his team win. UCF is one win away from a bowl game, snapping a two-year drought. Carter quarterbacks the defense, communicates adjustments when the offense audibles and shores up tackling. He led the team with 92 tackles last season and was on pace to continue wearing the crown until he got injured. UCF sorely missed his presence over the middle, but its depth stepped up. Tackett Curtis is the team's leading tackler with a career-high 67 tackles, two passes defended, two sacks and two interceptions. Jahleel Culbreath and Jayden Jennings have contributed alongside Curtis. They tallied 67 tackles, three pass deflections and 1.5 sacks. The Knights' front seven got its best linebacker back during a crucial Friday game against the Cyclones. Frost said they will be a " good challenge " with a dual-threat quarterback and the Big 12's leading rusher. Aiden Flora leads with 1,335 yards and is second with 12 touchdowns. Flora has tallied five 150-plus-yard games and four multi-touchdown games. He rushed for a career-high 221 yards in a 51-49 upset over the then-No. 24 Oklahoma State Cowboys and reached a career-best three touchdowns twice: once in a 45-42 win over the West Virginia Mountaineers and in a 41-13 blowout over the Cincinnati Bearcats. picks.headline: Nebraska Football vs. Ohio State Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Nebraska Football vs. Ohio State Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Can Nebraska finally beat a ranked team under Matt Rhule? The Huskers get their shot against Ohio State in Lincoln on Senior Day. It’s the last home game of the year, and a win would change how a lot of fans feel about this season. On the Carriker Chronicles, Adam Carriker breaks down why Nebraska has a chance, what worries him most, and why he thinks this game could still be up for grabs in the fourth quarter. Nebraska’s shutout of Rutgers showed how good this defense can be. The running game also put together a complete performance, which gives the Huskers something to build on. But can they run the ball against Ohio State when the Buckeyes know it’s coming? Carriker wants Nebraska to run with a purpose and give Anthony Colandrea some quick answers in the passing game. Get the tight ends involved. Take a few shots downfield when the matchup is there. And when it’s third down, give Ohio State something it hasn’t already seen. At some point, somebody has to win a one-on-one matchup. The biggest question on defense is Jeremiah Smith. How does Rob Aurich keep a receiver that good from taking over the game? That job gets tougher with Andrew Marshall out. Carriker talks through how Nebraska can mix up its pressure and make Ohio State work for its yards. A couple of big plays can undo an otherwise good afternoon for the defense. The Huskers need to keep Smith from getting loose and give themselves a chance to get off the field on third down. Carriker also spends time on something that could decide a close game: where each team starts with the ball. Archie Wilson can help Nebraska by pinning Ohio State deep and making the Buckeyes drive the length of the field. A turnover could give the Huskers a short field, but Nebraska has to cash in when it gets to the red zone. And if the defense or special teams can put seven points on the board themselves, that changes what the offense has to do to win. Carriker’s four keys are to win in the margins, limit what Ohio State does best, win the fourth quarter, and score a touchdown on defense or special teams. He sees a real path to an upset with the way Nebraska’s defense has played, the progress in the run game, and a home crowd that wants to send the seniors out with a win. In the end, the Huskers have yet to show us they can put together four full quarters against a team as good as Ohio State and the Jeremiah Smith matchup and Marshall’s absence are hard for him to get past. Carriker’s final score prediction is Ohio State 20, Nebraska 17. Published Nov 18, 2026 ADAM CARRIKER Adam’s dream of playing for the Huskers came to fruition. He was twice named first-team All-Big 12, leading the conference in sacks and winning the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year award his senior season, along with several other awards, including finishing with All-America honors, in addition to being named to the Big 12 Commissioner’s Academic Honor Roll three times. He’s also been named to Nebraska’s All-Century Team, voted The Best Husker Defensive End since the start of the new millennium, and has been inducted into the Nebraska Football Hall of Fame. Adam went on to play eight years as a Defensive Lineman in the NFL with the St. Louis Rams and Washington Redskins. He was drafted in the 1st round, winning Rams Rookie of the Year; he’s the only Ram in franchise history to start all 16 games as a rookie. He also won the Strongest Redskin award multiple times during his career in the NFL. Since retiring, he’s experienced great success in the business world and has also appeared multiple times on National Television and Radio Shows, and currently hosts his highly popular show, the Carriker Chronicles, aka, the People’s Show, which has been viewed by millions! away.blurb: Starting defenders Andrew Marshall, Jahsear Whittington, and Owen Chambliss are listed as out against Ohio State in the Huskers' Wednesday availability report. While Marshall's absence was expected , there was hope that Whittington and Chambliss could return. Instead, Nebraska will head into its final home game of 2026 without its best cover corner, top-graded linebacker, and current leader in sacks. Marshall, who earned Midseason All-America recognition from On3 and Sports Illustrated, is out for the year after undergoing surgery last week. He finished his senior campaign with 28 tackles, six pass deflections, one tackle for loss, and an interception. Marshall started Nebraska's first nine games before his injury occurred. Chambliss, who missed NU's season opener against Ohio, had been playing at a high level since his return. The San Diego State transfer was injured again against Illinois , though, playing just 31 defensive snaps in the Huskers' 24-13 loss in Champaign. Before suffering an injury against Indiana on Oct. 17, the junior had thrown for 2,007 yards and 19 touchdowns with just four interceptions. home.headline: Nebraska’s OSU injury report is rough, but Anthony Jones' return could be bright spot
home.blurb: Defensive back Andrew Marshall is out , as Matt Rhule announced earlier this week that one of the nation's top cornerbacks will miss the rest of Nebraska’s season. The good news for the Huskers is that defensive lineman Anthony Jones Jr. was upgraded from “out” last week to “questionable” this week. With this being the first injury report of the week, there’s now hope that he could be upgraded to probable by Friday and then suit up on Saturday morning. For Ohio State, the guys who are out were all expected to be out. Quarterback Julian Sayin, running back Ja'Kobi Jackson, safety Deshawn Stewart, wide receiver Brennen Schramm, offensive linemen Jaxon Powell and Max Riley, and tight end Maxence LeBlanc will miss the game against the Cornhuskers. Nebraska football loses Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington but Anthony Jones could return The Ohio State players who are questionable are safety Terry Moore, wide receiver Brock Boyd, safety Brenten "Inky" Jones, linebacker Eli Lee, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels. The biggest piece of positive news for the Buckeyes is that senior left guard Luke Montgomery is expected to return. Montgomery is ready to roll after not appearing on the report, while both Daniels and Boyd are listed as questionable. Montgomery and Daniels had flu-like symptoms last week, while Boyd has been battling a sprained ankle for more than a month. No surprises popped up on the availability report for Ohio State, unlike last week when Montgomery was initially listed as questionable. That suggests the Buckeyes avoided any major new injuries in their win over Northwestern. Of course, the biggest absence of all for OSU is quarterback Julian Sayin. That might not be as big a problem for Ryan Day and company after his replacement, Luke Fahey , finally had a very solid outing. Against Northwestern, Fahey completed 21 of 32 passes for 201 yards and 3 touchdowns. He also threw an interception, but the biggest step forward was that he seemed to figure out a secret to the offense: Just get the ball to Jeremiah Smith. Without Owen Chambliss, Jahsear Whittington, and Andrew Marshall, Nebraska will have its work cut out for it on Saturday morning. picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet
picks.blurb: 3 Bold Predictions for Wisconsin vs. Purdue: Don't Count out Colton Joseph Just Yet Skip to main content SI.COM WISCONSIN ATHLETICS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS FOOTBALL BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM BADGERS BASKETBALL As the Badgers' seesaw of a 2026 season rolls on, Wisconsin once finds itself on the wrong end of a tough loss after collapsing on the road against Maryland . Sitting at 6-4 (4-3 in the B1G), head coach Luke Fickell and company are running out of time to prove that they're guiding this program in the right direction. A resounding win over an inferior opponent , bouncing back from a mind-numbing loss in the process, would be a great start. I've got three bold predictions for the Badgers' clash with the Boilermakers in West Lafayette. Colton Joseph recaptures the hearts of Badgers fans Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. Ryan Hopkins is currently listed as questionable this week, but the early indications are that Joseph is going to re-assume the QB1 role after Hopkins took a huge blindside hit and had to be helped off the field late in the loss to Maryland. If Joseph indeed gets the starting nod in place of an injured Hopkins, it's not hard to see him playing well and in the process, winning back the hearts of some Badgers fans despite his well-documented struggles this season. First of all, Joseph should have no shortage of motivation. He was benched for a true freshman, and now gets his shot to prove that was a big mistake. That's a situation any competitor dreams of, and say what you will about Joseph; he's certainly a competitor. What's more, after getting benched for Hopkins and with the future of the entire coaching staff potentially up in the air this offseason, Joseph needs to put good things on tape should he be forced to enter the transfer portal again this winter. At best, he's proved dynamic yet inconsistent at the Big Ten level and at worst, he's been a turnover machine with limited arm talent. If Hopkins is forced to sit out one or both of the final two games this fall, these contests are massively important for Joseph's future; how he plays could determine whether he remains at the Power Four level in 2027. Finally, Purdue's defense is extremely permeable . It has the worst total defense in the Big Ten (417.3 yards per game) and the second-worst passing defense in the conference (239.0 yards per game). Purdue struggles to get consistent pressure (13 sacks across 10 games) and doesn't force turnovers with regularity. If there's any defense for Joseph to carve through, it's the Boilermakers. Purdue Boilermakers quarterback Ryan Browne. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Purdue's Ryan Browne is second in the Big Ten and 20th nationally with 2,418 passing yards. Though Purdue scores 27.2 points per game, a meager 76th in the country, its quarterback has been a bright spot in terms of offensive production. Still, dive into Browne's performance this season, and the numbers are a tad misleading. The quarterback hasn't eclipsed 300 passing yards since Week 3 against UCLA, and while that's certainly an impressive feat given how strong the Bruins' defense is, he's struggled pretty mightily against the other top defenses he's faced. In fact, Browne has been held under 160 passing yards in four of his last seven outings. Against the top passing defenses he's played such as Penn State (No. 3 nationally in passing yards allowed per game) as well as Iowa and Minnesota (both of whom rank inside the top-45 in passing yards allowed), he's had a rough go of it. The Nittany Lions held him to 142 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on 34 percent completion. Iowa limited him to 158 yards, one touchdown and one interceptions. And while Purdue blew out Minnesota, Brown only collected 159 passing yards, one score and 58 percent completion. Wisconsin's pass defense, meanwhile, checks in at No. 25 in the country. And while it just allowed Maryland's backup to complete 21-of-23 passes last week, the Badgers' defense has managed to bounce back from its poor performances this season. It'll need to run it back in West Lafayette. The Badgers' offensive line looks passable This might be the boldest prediction of the three, considering how much of a struggle its been up front for Wisconsin. Last week against Maryland, the Badgers' offensive line struggled mightily in pass protection, allowing four sacks. It wasn't much better in the run game, as Wisconsin backs created just 3.3 yards per carry and also suffered six tackles-for-loss. Still, Maryland's lowly record did well to disguise just how capable its front seven actually is. For how bad the Terps have been this fall, their defensive front is pretty loaded with capable playmakers. The same can't be said for Purdue. The Boilermakers have just 13 sacks on the season, firmly placing them into the bottom tier of teams; only 14 FBS programs have fewer. They've created 107 total pressures, which is harder to contextualize nationally but compared with Wisconsin's 145 total pressures, they're a clear step down. Their run defense, meanwhile, surrenders 178.3 yards per game, good for 110th nationally. Their defense as a whole has collected 205 stops, or tackles that constitute a failure for the offense, compared to Wisconsin's 276. Translation? They don't penetrate the backfield or win at the point of attack nearly as well as the Badgers. Despite what could be a patchwork offensive line this week, I still expect Wisconsin to find success up front. The undefeated fifth-ranked Boilermakers led No. 10 Wisconsin 17-14 in a nationally televised game (back when that wasn't the norm) and with ESPN College Gameday set up on campus. Kyle Orton ran a naked bootleg on third down, seemingly keeping the drive alive for Purdue to burn more clock, only Orton was hit, jarring the ball loose. Scott Starks picked it up and returned it 40 yards for a touchdown. After Bernard Pollard blocked the extra point, the Boilers drove into field goal range but missed a game-tying field goal attempt in the final minute. Wisconsin escaped Ross-Ade Stadium with a 20-17 victory , its first in what is now a string of 18 consecutive Badger victories in the series. On Saturday, Purdue coach Barry Odom gets his first chance to end more than two decades of coming up on the wrong side against the Badgers . "The great thing is this team had nothing to do with that. But it is history. I What to knthink you always learn from those things. You take those things and use it as needed or as you think your current team needs." Odom's timeframe is off. He was a sophomore linebacker at Missouri when Purdue defeated Wisconsin 45-20 at Ross-Ade Stadium in 1997, but his point was made. It's been a long time. What to know about Purdue football's opponent, Wisconsin The Badgers are 6-4, coming off a loss to Maryland in what has been an up-and-down season that includes a 24-7 win over USC on Oct. 24. Wisconsin allows just 17 points per game, problematic for a Purdue offense that has both looked phenomenal and, more recently, shown an inability to capitalize in the red zone. Wisconsin is allowing just 2.8 yards per carry this season, aided by the Badgers' 20 sacks. Oct 16, 2026; West Lafayette, Indiana, USA; Washington Huskies linebacker Taariq al-Uqdah (0) is tackled by Purdue Boilermakers linebacker Jojo Hayden (0) during the second half at Ross-Ade Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Marc Lebryk-Imagn Images What is undetermined is who'll line up behind center against Purdue. Quarterback Ryan Hopkins was injured on a strip sack late in a loss on Nov. 14 against Maryland, setting up the Terrapins' game-winning field goal. Hopkins is listed as questionable entering Saturday's game. Hopkins was elevated to starting quarterback to replace the struggling Colton Joseph two weeks ago. WISCONSIN STATISTICAL LEADERS − Passing: Colton Joseph (106-189, 1,368 yards, 11 TD, 5 INT), Ryan Hopkins (37-59, 411 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT). Rushing: Abu Sama III (68 car., 373 yards, 1 TD), Joseph (91 car., 371 yards, 4 TD). Receiving: Tyrell Henry (36 rec., 434 yards, 1 TD), Jacob Harris (20 rec., 347 yards, 4 TD). Tackles: Cooper Catalano (100), Mason Posa (86). Tackles for loss: Sebastian Cheeks (9), Posa (7.5). Sacks: Cheeks (7). Interceptions: Marvin Burks Jr. (2). Kicking: Gavin Lahm (15-17 FG, long of 51). Punting: Sean West (39 punts, 43.3 average). Purdue football players to watch Antonio Harris began the season as Purdue's fourth running back. Meanwhile, he became a special teams standout while also slowly working his way up the running back depth chart. During Purdue's four-game losing streak, Harris is averaging 10.1 yards per carry, but has only taken 15 handoffs. For the season, Harris leads Purdue with 6.8 yards per carry and has not had a negative yardage run. With Fame Ijeboi not producing at the clip he had earlier in the season, offensive coordinator Josh Henson could lean more on the flourishing Harris to revive a struggling rushing attack. Despite falling behind early at Iowa, Purdue's defense finally showed some semblance of a pass rush in its first week without Kevin Kane leading the defense. Keyshawn Burgos had a breakout performance with three tackles, a sack and a blocked field goal. Will the Virginia Tech transfer's productivity carry over against Wisconsin? PURDUE STATISTICAL LEADERS − Passing: Ryan Browne (193-311, 2,418 yards, 12 TD, 6 INT). Rushing: Fame Ijeboi (175 car., 684 yards, 10 TD), Antonio Harris (38 car., 242 yards, 2 TD). Receiving: Asaad Waseem (49 rec., 802 yards, 1 TD), Xavier Townsend (44 rec., 477 yards, 3 TD). Tackles: Jojo Hayden (77), Charles Correa (68), Justin Denson Jr. (66). Tackles for loss: Correa (5), Jeremy Lewis (3.5). Sacks: Curt Neal (2.5), Keyshawn Burgos (2.5). Interceptions: Jojo Hayden (2). Kicking: Jacobo Echeverria Lozano (21-23 FG, long of 49, 27-27 PAT). Punting: Dylan Drennan (39 punts, 44.8 average). What uniform combination will Purdue wear vs. Wisconsin Purdue will wear black helmets with black jerseys and gold pants against Wisconsin. Purdue football honorary captain vs. Wisconsin Former Purdue quarterback Joey Elliott will serve as honorary captain against the Badgers. Elliott currently works in the Indianapolis Colts front office as assistant director of pro scouting. Elliott played for Purdue from 2006-09. In 2009 as a senior, Elliott threw for 3,026 yards and 22 touchdowns. Purdue football vs. Wisconsin prediction In a season where nothing makes sense, from the defensive coordinator hire to going to the wire against Wake Forest and UCLA (far more impressive now than it seemed then) to two surprising wins followed by a couple surprising losses, it's only fitting this would be the year this 18-game losing streak to the Badgers ends. The Wisconsin Badgers 6-4 (4-3) head into Ross-Ade to take on the Purdue Boilermakers 3-7 (2-5) at noon on Saturday. The Badgers have struggled in the last month as well. Wisconsin has lost three of its last five games, with its offense faltering against UCLA and Iowa, scoring a combined 7 points, and then letting one slip against Maryland last week. Purdue's offense, led by quarterback Ryan Browne, has been game most of the year, but it couldn't muster more than seven points against a tough Hawkeyes defense last week. Wisconsin is coming off its own disappointing road performance, falling to Maryland 24-21. Ryan Hopkins and the Badgers passing game never got going against the Terrapins. He connected on just half of his 22 pass attempts and had just 77 yards in the air. Purdue's defense has been a bit more generous towards offenses than most, but it'll be the run game of the Badgers that will be Purdue's primary focus. The Badgers have had a lot of success against Purdue over the recent years, dominating the line of scrimmage. Purdue will try to counter by leaning on Fame Ijeboi who has ran for nearly 700 yards this season. While Purdue don't have a bowl game to play for anymore, there's still plenty of pride and momentum to try and pick up at the end of Odom's second season in West Lafayette. It will be a battle of a faulty offense versus a sieve of a defense. If Purdue's offense can get working against the Badgers, there could certainly be a surprise showing of points between the two teams. Weather looks decent in West Lafayette if not a bit on the brisk side. It's that time of year where the end of the football season is coming. away.headline: Wisconsin football gets bad news on Javan Robinson, O-line from initial Purdue injury report
away.blurb: With two games to play in the regular season, however, that luck may be running out . Wisconsin's initial injury report lists starting cornerback and the Badgers' best cover man in the secondary, Javan Robinson, as doubtful for Saturday afternoon. That means barring a significant development, Wisconsin will be without its top cornerback and another veteran leader in the secondary. Starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins, who Fickell sounded encouraged about on Monday, is listed as questionable. Right now, it looks like a toss-up if he'll be able to play despite Fickell saying earlier in the week that "Hopefully he'll be fine...luckily it's not his throwing side." Wisconsin's starting right tackle Emerson Mandell is also listed as questionable. He wasn't noticeably banged up last week against the Terps, so Fickell wasn't asked about his status on Monday. However, he's now a question mark as well, and with Barrett Nelson also unavailable for the past three weeks, Wisconsin could be forced to start a tackle tandem of PJ Wilkins and Lucas Simmons-Johansson. That's certainly less than ideal, although the latter did just play a career-high 26 snaps against Maryland. Though Robinson almost certainly being out and the uncertainty around Hopkins and Mandell is disheartening, the Badgers did receive some good news on the injury front. Their other starting cornerback Jai'mier Scott, who didn't play last week in College Park, is listed as probable, as is star pass-rusher Sebastian Cheeks. Getting those two back would do wonders to mitigate the damage this defense has already suffered. Regardless of how the week shakes out, Wisconsin is going to have to take down Purdue somewhat short-handed. Wisconsin Football is Running Out of Time to Fix its Ground Game Other than the constant shuffling on the offensive line, much of which was caused at least initially by injuries suffered before the season began, Wisconsin football has had a relatively clean bill of health for much of the year, especially considering head coach Luke Fickell's past injury luck in Madison. When Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3 B1G) travels to face Purdue (3-7, 2-5 B1G) on Saturday afternoon in West Lafayette, it could be without several key starters in a game that's critically important for Fickell and company to bounce back and win after the late collapse in College Park last weekend. We already knew that starting safety Matt Jung was lost for the season, joining the likes of offensive tackle Kevin Heywood and cornerback Cai Bates. But the Badgers' initial injury report poses more questions than answers ahead of a game against Purdue in which, again, Wisconsin could really use a bounce-back victory on the road. away.headline: Ryan Hopkins headlines first Wisconsin vs. Purdue availability report
away.blurb: However, Luke Fickell and Co. didn’t just leave SECU Stadium with a bruised ego, as newly-donned starting quarterback Ryan Hopkins was recently listed as questionable in Wisconsin’s latest injury availability report ahead of this weekend’s clash against the Purdue Boilermakers . The Wisconsin Badgers are stumbling to the end of the 2026 football season, as their 24-21 loss against the Maryland Terrapins last weekend did them no favors. What does this mean for Wisconsin’s quarterback situation? In Hopkins’ two starts for the Badgers , the Mater Dei product tallied 318 yards through the air, on a 63% completion rate, along with three touchdowns and two fumbles. In Wisconsin’s last-second loss to the Terps, Hopkins finished with just 55 yards in the air, continuing a trend of disappointing quarterback play in 2026. If Hopkins is unable to go, it's plausible that original starter Colton Joseph gets the start, as the former Old Dominion quarterback has totaled 1,739 all-purpose yards, along with 15 total touchdowns and six turnovers. picks.headline: Matchup Preview and Final Score Prediction for Virginia vs. North Carolina
picks.blurb: Matchup Preview and Final Score Prediction for Virginia vs. North Carolina Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM CAVALIERS BB Virginia and North Carolina have played 130 times. The stakes for the 131st matchup are simple, as both teams are 5-5, and the winner becomes bowl-eligible. However, the loser of Saturday’s matchup will still get one more shot. North Carolina plays 4-6 NC State at home on Nov. 28, and Virginia travels to Blacksburg to face Franklin’s 6-4 Virginia Tech team. Saturday is the easier path for the Cavaliers on Senior Day. Bill Belichick hasn't announced who will play quarterback, and the Tar Heels will be without two of their best defenders for at least part of the afternoon. Why this game matters A win would send Virginia to a bowl game for the second straight season, which hasn't happened since 2018 and 2019. It isn't last year's 11-3 finish, but it would salvage a season that looked like it was slipping away less than a month ago. The Cavaliers lost three straight ACC games in October, bottoming out with a 51-7 blowout loss at Wake Forest. After the bye, they beat Cal 36-7, their largest-margin win in an ACC game under Tony Elliott, but the Hoos haven't won back-to-back games since opening the season against NC State and Norfolk State. "It's extremely important just for the mindset and mentality of our program," Elliott said Tuesday. "We're fortunate to be able to play two more games, right? And it doesn't matter who we play, when we play, where we play, what the circumstances are, what the record is." Homefield advantage could help. Virginia is 5-1 at Scott Stadium this season and has won 11 of its last 13 games there since the start of 2025. North Carolina has been the opposite: 1-4 at home and 3-1 on the road, with both of its ACC wins (Pitt and Duke) away from Chapel Hill. A win Saturday would be UNC's fourth straight road win. Recent history in Charlottesville doesn't favor the Hoos, though. UNC won its last two trips to Scott Stadium, 31-28 in 2022 and 41-14 in 2024, and Virginia hasn't beaten the Tar Heels at home since 2020. Elliott is 2-0 against UNC in Chapel Hill and 0-2 against them in Charlottesville. Last year's meeting was the 17-16 overtime win at Kenan Stadium that ended with Benjamin Hall stopped inches short on a two-point try. Virginia will honor about 50 upperclassmen before kickoff. The Cavaliers lead the country with 31 players in at least their fifth year of college, including seventh-year punter Daniel Sparks and kicker Will Bettridge, the program's all-time leading scorer. They arrived on Grounds in 2022, @Coach_TElliott 's first year with @UVAFootball , and each has become an integral part of the program. "The foundation that's been built, they laid it," Elliott says of five-year starters @Dsparks115 and @will_bettridge . https://t.co/2qUwjvTice Who's playing quarterback for North Carolina? Billy Edwards Jr. has taken the first snap in all 10 of UNC's games. He left last week's 16-14 loss to Louisville in the third quarter with what UNC's own game recap called an apparent upper-body injury, and he was still listed as questionable on Thursday night's availability report. Belichick has said UNC is taking Edwards' status day by day, and earlier in the week, he said Edwards was "getting better," according to WRAL. He hasn't named a starter, and the ACC's final availability report isn't due until two hours before kickoff. Edwards has completed 65.5% of his passes for 2,247 yards, 18 touchdowns, and six interceptions. He's a pocket passer. Counting sacks, he has zero net rushing yards on 51 carries. His best game came against then-No. 1 Miami, when he went 28 of 34 for 341 yards and four touchdowns in a 38-35 loss. If he can't go, it's likely Travis Burgess. The true freshman made his college debut against Louisville and went 6 of 11 for 59 yards with an interception. He also ran eight times for 35 yards, and UNC's game notes point out that he gained 52 yards on his five non-sack carries, four of which picked up first downs. If he starts, he'd be the first true freshman to start at quarterback for UNC in an ACC game since Sam Howell in 2019, according to the Fayetteville Observer. Belichick said Monday that UNC will have "the same offense" either way, though some plays get more emphasis with one quarterback than the other. Virginia's pass defense has carried this unit, but the run defense has been weaker. Opponents average 4.2 yards per carry against UVA, and 17 of the 25 touchdowns Virginia has allowed have come on the ground. The worst of it came at Florida State, where quarterback Ashton Daniels ran for five touchdowns in a 38-7 Seminoles win. North Carolina's run game hasn't scared many people this year. The Tar Heels average 114.2 rushing yards per game and 3.7 yards per carry. A quarterback who can pick up a third down with his legs changes that, and it would hand defensive coordinator John Rudzinski a different set of problems than Edwards does. Jelani Thurman vs. a thin linebacker room UNC will be looking for the same two targets. Receiver Jordan Shipp leads the Tar Heels with 57 catches for 703 yards. Tight end Jelani Thurman has 50 catches for 597 yards, and his eight touchdown catches tie the UNC single-season record for a tight end and lead all tight ends nationally. The 6-foot-6 Mackey Award semifinalist has at least three catches in every game this season and a team-high 328 yards after the catch. On paper, Virginia is built to handle a passing offense. The Cavaliers lead the ACC in pass defense (186.6 yards per game) and pass efficiency defense, and they've allowed only eight passing touchdowns all year. They also have 11 interceptions, including three against Cal. Two of those went back for touchdowns: Brandyn Hillman's 100-yard return and Kam Robinson's 33-yarder. The question is who covers the middle of the field. Linebacker Maddox Marcellus is out for the season after knee surgery, and fellow linebacker Landon Danley is also listed as out this week. Marcellus had 44 tackles and 4.5 tackles for loss in nine games. Danley has 29 tackles and two starts. Justin Rowe got the start in Marcellus' spot against Cal, the first of his career. He has 12 tackles this season and returned an interception 50 yards for a touchdown against Delaware. Myles Brown has played in all 10 games and has 34 tackles and three pass breakups, but he hasn't started a game this year. That's a lot to put on two backups against a tight end who is this good with the ball in his hands. Robinson (46 tackles, six tackles for loss, two interceptions) will need to be at his best in the middle, and Virginia at least has its safeties back. Hillman and Ethan Minter both returned from injuries against Cal. If Thurman has a big day, UNC can move the ball even without much of a running game. If Virginia's linebackers hold up, the Tar Heels have to find another way to beat the ACC's top pass defense. Can Virginia finish drives in the end zone? Virginia's defense has played well enough to win most weeks. The offense is definitely the bigger unknown, and the problems show up after it crosses the 20-yard line. UVA has scored touchdowns on 22 of 37 red zone trips (59%) and converted 43 of 136 third downs (32%). It has also gone for it on fourth down 34 times, converting 22. Even the Cal win followed the pattern. Virginia is 0-4 when it scores fewer than 21 points and 5-1 when it scores 21 or more. The passing game has narrowed since the start of the season. Pribula hasn't thrown more than one touchdown pass in a game since Sept. 26 against Delaware, and his last four have all gone to Da'Shawn Martin, who has seven touchdown catches this season. North Carolina's defense also gives up plenty on third down, as opponents convert 44% of the time, but it tightens up near the goal line. Teams have scored touchdowns on just 18 of 34 red zone trips against the Tar Heels (53%). Elliott liked what he saw from his line against Cal. "I thought [we] dominated the line of scrimmage. ... So, I thought there was a lot of progress," he said Tuesday. "I thought the quarterback came out clean, didn't get hit much." That will be harder to repeat against Xavier Lewis. The sophomore defensive tackle has 44 tackles, 10 tackles for loss and seven sacks, and he's a Bednarik Award semifinalist, the first Tar Heel to make that list since Julius Peppers in 2001. Virginia has allowed 28 sacks this season, and its interior line is in flux. Center Drake Metcalf is questionable, and against Cal, Noah Josey moved from left guard to center with Ben York starting at left guard. UNC will be without the other half of its pass rush. Defensive end Melkart Abou Jaoude, who had three sacks in last year's game, is out with a broken right hand. He has two sacks and a team-high nine quarterback hurries this season. The run game is Virginia's best way to stay ahead of the chains. UNC allows 4.0 yards per carry and 149.6 rushing yards per game, and the Cavaliers ran for 201 yards against Cal. Jekail Middlebrook (540 yards, 4.9 per carry) is listed as the starter after missing the Wake Forest game and getting a light workload on the ground against Cal. Solomon Beebe has also started to see more of the ball. "He probably has the most juice of all the [running backs], he's got the home run potential," Elliott said of Beebe. The first is turnovers. Virginia has given the ball away six times all season (three interceptions, three lost fumbles), tied for seventh-fewest nationally. The Cavaliers have forced 12 turnovers and outscored opponents 45-9 in points off turnovers. North Carolina is -3 in turnover margin. The Tar Heels have lost seven of their eight fumbles, and they're 0-4 in games where they haven't forced a turnover. Safety Greg Smith III, who has a team-high three interceptions, will sit out the first half after the ACC suspended him for his role in the postgame fight against Louisville. Sparks is a true X-Factor as he leads the nation at 50.6 yards per punt, and 21 of his 43 punts have pinned opponents inside the 20. Even after returns, Virginia nets 42.8 yards per punt to UNC's 38.1. In a game where both offenses could have trouble finishing drives, a few extra yards on every exchange add up. UNC does have a weapon in the return game. Freshman Jaden Jefferson took a kickoff 98 yards for a touchdown against ranked Notre Dame on his first college touch. Keys, prediction for Tar Heels vs Cavaliers Rodd Baxley, Fayetteville Observer · The Fayetteville Observer Fri, November 20, 2026 at 10:05 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads UNC football has two more opportunities to secure bowl eligibility in its second season under coach Bill Belichick . The next chance comes in the latest edition of "The South's Oldest Rivalry" as the Tar Heels (5-5, 2-4 ACC) travel to Virginia (5-5, 3-4) for an ACC game at Scott Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21. Kickoff is set for 12:30 p.m. and the game will be televised on The CW . Watch UNC-Virginia on Fubo BOWL PROJECTIONS: Will UNC football make postseason? Latest bowl projections before Virginia game INJURY REPORT: Who is on UNC football vs Virginia injury report? Latest from ACC availability report POSTGAME BRAWL: ACC announces suspensions, fines for UNC football and Louisville after postgame fight UNC has a 4-1 record away from Chapel Hill this season, including a season-opening win against TCU in Ireland. The Tar Heels have won three straight road games since a mid-September loss at Clemson. UNC has also won consecutive games on Virginia's home field. If it stretches that streak to three, it would be the first time since 2016. Overall, the Tar Heels have a 28-27 record at Virginia. Here are some stats to know, players to watch and a score prediction for the Tar Heels vs. Cavaliers. Billy Edwards or Travis Burgess as UNC quarterback vs Virginia? Who will be UNC's starting quarterback vs. Virginia? That's the biggest question surrounding this game. A sixth-year player who started the first 10 games of the season, Billy Edwards Jr. was listed as questionable on the initial ACC availability report . That could open the door for freshman QB Travis Burgess to get his first career start. Burgess replaced Edwards in the second half of the Tar Heels' loss to Louisville, leading a late scoring drive that gave UNC an opportunity to win in the fourth quarter. If Burgess does get the start, he would be the first true freshman to start at QB for UNC in an ACC game since Sam Howell in 2019. UNC defense faces challenge vs Virginia QB Beau Pribula without Greg Smith UNC's defense is arguably coming off its best performance of the season, limiting a Louisville offense that averaged more than 40 points per game to 16 at Kenan Stadium. The Tar Heels won't face that level of explosiveness against Virginia, but it could be tough because of the absence of two key players. Defensive back Greg Smith and defensive lineman Melkart Abou Jaoude are among the Tar Heels out vs. the Cavaliers, but Smith is only out for the first half for his role in the postgame brawl vs. Louisville. In Virginia's wins, quarterback Beau Pribula is averaging 171 passing yards and 45 rushing yards with 11 passing TDs, one rushing TD and one interception. In five losses, Pribula is averaging 174 passing yards and 7 rushing yards with four passing TDs, two interceptions and a rushing TD. If UNC can bottle up Pribula, it'll likely leave Charlottesville its sixth win of the season. UNC running back Benjamin Hall gets redemption shot vs Virginia Benjamin Hall was just short of the goal line on a two-point conversion that would have given UNC its first signature win under Bill Belichick in 2025. The Tar Heels lost 17-16 to No. 16 Virginia in overtime last season at Kenan Stadium . With three touchdowns in the last two weeks, including a two-TD effort vs. Louisville, Hall will have a chance at redemption on Saturday at Scott Stadium. The junior running back's two best games of the season came on the road. Hall logged 130 rushing yards and a receiving TD at Clemson and racked up 81 rushing yards and a TD on nine carries at UConn. UNC vs Virginia score prediction UNC 22, Virginia 18: The Tar Heels have been a different team on the road this season, finding ways to win by creating takeaways and scoring on explosive plays. Even with its questions at QB, UNC seems to get a jolt away from Chapel Hill. Belichick's boys will be celebrating in Charlottesville after securing bowl eligibility ahead of the regular-season finale. Virginia finally put together a convincing performance against Cal, and congratulations on that, but one good Saturday doesn't erase how rough conference play has been for the Cavaliers. North Carolina hasn't exactly been reliable at home, either. The difference is that the Tar Heels have actually played some of their best football away from Chapel Hill, and I think that travels to Charlottesville. North Carolina is 3-1 in true road games, with wins at Pitt, Duke and UConn. The Pitt and Duke wins came by four points apiece, and the Tar Heels followed them with a 38-21 victory at UConn. That's not a murderer's row, but winning three straight road games is hard to dismiss when we're talking about a matchup priced essentially as a toss-up. Compare that with North Carolina's recent home form: losses to Syracuse, Miami and Louisville in three of its last four games. The results haven't always been pretty, but the road version of this team has been more dependable. Virginia's 36-7 win over Cal looks great on the scoreboard, although it's worth remembering that two of the Cavaliers' touchdowns came on interception returns. That was a much-needed response after losing three straight to SMU, Duke and Wake Forest, including a 51-7 beating at Wake. I've been waiting for Virginia's veteran offensive line to become a consistent strength, but it hasn't happened. The Cavaliers have struggled to protect Beau Pribula and are converting only about 32 percent of third downs. That's a major problem against a North Carolina defense that just showed it can make a good offense work. The Tar Heels lost 16-14 to Louisville last week, but I thought the defense deserved a lot more credit than the final result suggests. Louisville came in averaging more than 40 points and nearly eight yards per play. North Carolina held the Cardinals to 302 yards, just 4.7 per play, and only one gain of more than 20 yards. Derek McDonald has been all over the field with 101 tackles on the season. If that defense shows up again, Virginia isn't suddenly going to find easy yards just because it's playing its home finale. There is one legitimate concern for North Carolina, and that's the quarterback situation. Billy Edwards Jr. left the Louisville game injured and was listed as questionable, while freshman Travis Burgess came in and showed some mobility but also threw an interception. I'm not going to pretend that uncertainty doesn't matter. Still, Virginia has been vulnerable to mobile quarterbacks, and Burgess at least gives the Tar Heels a different way to move the chains if he's needed. North Carolina is also converting around 46 percent of its third downs, compared with Virginia's much lower rate, which is a meaningful difference in a game where possessions could be limited. Virginia is 5-1 at Scott Stadium, and this is Senior Day, so the Cavaliers absolutely have a home-field argument. Pribula can hurt opponents with his legs, too, and Virginia's plus-six turnover margin is better than North Carolina's minus-three. Those are real reasons this isn't a slam dunk. But the Cavaliers have struggled to finish drives, scoring on roughly 73 percent of their red-zone trips, while North Carolina has converted better than 90 percent of its opportunities. With neither offense consistently explosive, missed chances inside the twenty could matter as much as the occasional big play. The Tar Heels announced Tuesday that Avdalas underwent surgery to repair the injury. The sophomore suffered the injury during Friday night’s 78-70 loss to Georgia at the Dean E. Smith Center. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. The injury is a tough blow for first-year head coach Michael Malone, who has relied on Avdalas as an important part of the Tar Heels’ backcourt rotation. He also recorded 15 assists, the most on the team, while ranking fourth in scoring. Avdalas started all four games for the Tar Heels after transferring from Virginia Tech during the offseason. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. His size, versatility and playmaking ability made him an important addition to Malone’s first North Carolina roster. Tar Heels Must Adjust Without Neo Avdalas With Avdalas sidelined, North Carolina will need other players to take on additional responsibilities in the backcourt. Terrence Brown, Isaiah Denis, Angelo Brizzi and Jaydon Young could all see increased opportunities as the Tar Heels look to replace Avdalas’ production and playmaking. Brown has been one of North Carolina’s leading offensive contributors early in the season, while Denis has also provided valuable minutes in the backcourt. North Carolina enters the next stretch of its schedule at 3-1 following the loss to Georgia. The Tar Heels will look to get back on track when they host Marshall on Friday, Nov. 20. His absence will be an early test for Malone and the Tar Heels as they attempt to maintain momentum and navigate the opening portion of their ACC schedule without one of their key offseason additions. My UCLA vs. Michigan prediction has me laying the number with the road favorite, as the Bruins hold a trench advantage over the struggling Wolverines. Week 12 sends No. 4 UCLA (10-0, 7-0 Big Ten) to Michigan (5-5, 2-5 Big Ten) on Saturday, Nov. 21, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS from Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor. The Bruins are 3.5-point favorites at Kalshi, with a total of 36.5 and moneyline probabilities of 64% for UCLA and 42% for Michigan. More importantly, the Bruins have a better line-yards-per-snap average on both sides of the ball and a higher standard-down EPA-per-play differential, per College Football Data . Those are two of my favorite predictive metrics because controlling the trenches and staying ahead of schedule usually travels. UCLA vs Michigan Over/Under pick: Under 36.5 It's Under 36.5, down to 35.5 , or pass. These teams are built for a rock-fight . The Wolverines rank 116th nationally in seconds per play , and somehow, UCLA is even slower at 124th . The Bruins have the nation's 17th-highest rushing rate, with Michigan coming in at 20th. Per GameOnPaper , both defenses are better at limiting explosive plays than their offenses are at producing them. Michigan's scoring unit is especially boring, ranking in the 15th percentile nationally in explosive play rate. A slow tempo, heavy rushing, and limited big-play potential make the Under my play. UCLA vs Michigan combo Michigan playing from behind is the entire point here. UCLA doesn't need an offensive masterpiece, just enough early control to force the Wolverines out of their comfort zone. Their offense is terrible, and the methodical Bruins have no reason to speed things up with a lead. That's the game script tying these three plays together: UCLA takes charge, Michigan sputters, and the clock becomes the Bruins' best friend. Pretty football? Absolutely not. (Photo by Steven King/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan football season felt over when the Wolverines lost to Michigan State, and that defeat seems to have had a similar impact on the team. Michigan lost on the road against Oregon, 31-7, last weekend, and it didn't look like anyone was mentally present for the Wolverines. This weekend presents a new challenge — the UCLA Bruins. UCLA is having a special season, especially considering this was one of the worst teams in the Big Ten last year. The Bruins are 10-0 and knocking on the doorstep of the Big Ten Championship and College Football Playoff. A win this weekend would clinch the Bruins a spot in Indy, and it would likely make it impossible for them to miss the CFP. Somehow, UCLA is only favored by 3.5 points leading up to this game. Does Vegas know something, or will it be another uninspiring performance from the Wolverines? Let's make some bold predictions for the game. Michigan will go to another backup QB The Oregon game was interesting, as Michigan went back-and-forth between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood, waiting for someone to provide a spark. The thing is, I really don't think it matters. I don't think the issue is with the quarterbacks at all, as I think Underwood and Carr have both shown some good flashes. I believe the real issue boils down to poor offensive line play and the refusal to involve the tight ends more. Still, the coaches are going to search for a spark. Brayden Fowler-Nicolosi, a transfer from Colorado State, should be next in line at the quarterback position. I'm honestly surprised we haven't seen him yet, but there's truly nothing to lose at this point. Give him a shot. Michigan gets shutout I don't like to reuse predictions in these, but I'm honestly shocked this hasn't happened yet and I feel like it's inevitable at this point. This offense has amazed us with levels of bad we didn't know existed, and I think it still has one more trick up its sleeve. UCLA is 10-0 in large part due to its defense. Remember, the Bruins have been without starting quarterback Nico Iamaleava since Oct. 10 when he got hurt at Oregon. Since then, only one team has hit 20 points against the Bruins. They are ranked No. 4 in the country in total defense. UCLA is shutting everyone down. Michigan barely avoided a shutout against Michigan State, a bad team with a bad defense. Still, I just can't imagine the Wolverines finding any success offensively, and I would be shocked if UCLA doesn't easily cover the spread. Michigan's bowl hopes will hinge on The Game.

The football program's last title was the 1998 Pac-10 Championship, won in the regular season. Now, in just its third year as a Big Ten school, UCLA can go to the Big Ten Championship game with one more win in its last two games. Michigan is looking for anything positive at this point. The season crashed through the floor, going 2-5 in Big Ten play – losing to Oregon and Michigan State by a combined score of 46-13 – and now it needs a win in the last two games just to go to a bowl game. UCLA vs Michigan: Quick Hits Michigan closes with a bang: losing to Oregon 31-7 last week in Eugene, hosting UCLA this week, and finishing with the showdown against Ohio State in Columbus. UCLA closes at USC next week. It won't need the win if it can beat the Wolverines, but obviously, it's the rivalry game the Bruins want. The two teams haven't played since 2000, a 23-20 UCLA win. Starting in 1956 with a 42-13 win, UCLA is 8-3 in the series. How To Watch UCLA vs Michigan Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor, MI – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 250 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why UCLA Will Win Michigan doesn't do that whole scoring thing the kids are all into now. It was bad, there was a false ray of hope when Tommy Carr had a terrific day against a miserable Rutgers defense, and then everything got exponentially worse against Michigan State and Oregon. The Wolverines averaged 301 yards per game – 131st in the nation – and can't score even when they get into the red zone. But that's not the real problem. Michigan has turned it over multiple times in every game except for the wins over Oklahoma and Rutgers, and gave it away once in the loss to Iowa. It turned it over 13 times in the last six games. UCLA is No. 1 in the nation with 30 takeaways. Why Michigan Will Win UCLA isn't the type of team that wings the ball all over the yard. It's a tough, hard-nosed team, but it's not going to run away and hide with a big offensive explosion. The Bruins will play exactly the way Michigan wants. UCLA will need to run the ball, keep the tempo low, and rely on the lines – fine with the Wolverines. This is where the Wolverines can play it tough on the lines, work the field position battle, and try to keep this tight into the final few minutes. Despite the issues over the rough run, the defense is still among the ten best in America. UCLA vs Michigan Prediction, Betting Lines UCLA will have to work for it, but the defense will come up with the stop it needs late against the punchless Michigan offense. The Wolverines will come out fired up and cranked for the moment, marching down the field with a stunningly crisp opening scoring drive. But UCLA doesn't panic. The Bruin defense will be a rock on third downs, the offense will take the field goals and points when they're available, and Michigan's offense won't be able to take care of its opportunities to pull off the upset. It was the Tigers' fourth loss of the season, they're out of the College Football Playoff mix, and now it's time to play the spoiler role. Kiffin gets to play the villain, going back to his old coaching grounds – he was the Tennessee head coach in 2009 – and Tennessee will be fired up. The Vols are 8-2 after winning five of their last six games, and at No. 9 in the latest rankings, they're all but in the CFP if they win their last two games. LSU vs Tennessee: Quick Hits LSU closes out on the road at Arkansas after this. Lose to the Vols, and it'll be the third year in a row the program suffered a three-game losing streak. Tennessee goes to Vanderbilt to finish up the regular season. If it wins the final two games, it's in the mix for the SEC Championship along with the CFP. The two programs haven't met since 2022 – a 40-13 Tennessee win. LSU has won five of the last six, going back to 2005. How To Watch LSU vs Tennessee Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, TN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why LSU Will Win The talent is still there, the coaching is still great, and now the pressure is off. LSU isn't going anywhere this season, and now it can be Lane Unleashed as the team throws everything at a Vols team with all of the weight on its side of the field. The defense is the best in the SEC, the offense is the best in the SEC, the team holds the ball longer than anyone else in the conference, and no one in America generates more sacks. Tennessee has a problem keeping defenses out of the backfield, and now, here come the Tigers. Why Tennessee Will Win LSU might generate the most sacks in America, but Tennessee can bring the heat, too – the Tigers are No. 2 in sacks. It didn't sack Marcel Reed in last week's 22-7 win over Texas A&M, but it gave him a rough time. Now the Vols are back at home, where they take their defensive production up several notches. The defense has allowed just one touchdown pass in five games in Neyland, but in this, it's about the Tennessee run defense. LSU is 1-3 when running for fewer than 140 yards. Auburn and Furman – the Vols called off the dogs against the Paladins – are the only teams to hit the 140-yard mark. LSU vs Tennessee Prediction, Betting Lines Here's the thing about LSU this season. It pounces on the weak, but its best win is … at Auburn? That's good, but there really isn't a second-best victory going 0-4 against the current CFP-ranked teams on the slate. Tennessee is a top team. This might not be the sexiest team going, but it's got grit. It's a tough defensive team that doesn't make a ton of mistakes, and it doesn't get rattled. LSU will be terrific, but like the Kentucky and Texas games, it'll crumble late in the final moments. Now LSU travels to Tennessee , and what would've been a resume-strengthening game, has turned into a game that LSU can play spoiler in. Tennessee sits at 8-2 and ranked No. 9 in the College Football Playoff rankings, and a loss would tumble the Volunteers out of the running for a playoff spot. With LSU having no major post season games to play for, it's looking to play spoiler. LSU was so close to taking down Texas, and even Alabama, but a few key mistakes prevented it from winning. LSU has shown it hasn't fixed those problems, especially in the red zone, if LSU does show up and fix those problems in any game, it wins. That's what holds LSU out of the playoffs. LSU ranks No. 1 in adjusted EPA/play, No. 10 in net yards, No. 8 in total offense, No. 5 in total defense, No. 13 in point differential and No. 8 in SRS, which is strength of schedule and point differential. LSU is a good team. But costly mistakes in the red zone, like six interceptions, will crush your chances to win. But if LSU shows up and has its issues fixed, it will be the better team in Neyland this weekend. If not, that's up in the air. LSU's Advantages Nov 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers wide receiver Jackson Harris (4) runs the ball during the second half against Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium. But Tennessee has a problem coming to town: Jackson Harris. Harris has emerged as one of the best receivers in the country, just recently being named to the Biletnikoff semi-finalist list. Harris has been great inside, outside, short and deep for LSU, and has been a problem for defense after the catch and in the air. Tennessee cannot afford another slow defensive start, like its had sometimes this season, and Harris will torch the Vols. But Tennessee has to be the most careful at the line of scrimmage. LSU is home to a scary pass rush, and with Tennessee having some protection problems this season, the Tigers are ready to pounce on that. LSU is coming off of its most aggressive game yet, relentlessly pressuring Texas. LSU got after Arch Manning and forced three turnovers and a plethora of other broken plays and spoiled schemes. LSU needs to lean on its strengths to make the Vols uncomfortable. Mike Ianniello · Action Network Sat, November 21, 2026 at 10:43 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The LSU Tigers take on the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville, Tennessee, on Saturday, Nov. 21. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. LSU is favored by -1.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -115. Tennessee, meanwhile, enters as a +1.5 underdog and is +105 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 45.5 total points. Here's my LSU vs. Tennessee prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 21. LSU vs. Tennessee Pick: Tennessee ML (Play to -110) My Tennessee vs. LSU best bet is on the Volunteers to win outright. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . LSU vs Tennessee Odds LSU vs Tennessee point spread : LSU -1.5 (-105), Tennessee +1.5 (-115) LSU vs Tennessee over/under : 45.5 (-112o / -108u) LSU vs Tennessee moneyline : LSU -115, Tennessee -105 For a school that expects to be competing for National Championships every season, LSU's first year under Lane Kiffin has not gone as planned. A last-minute loss to Texas last week dropped the Tigers to 6-4 and knocked them out of the College Football Playoff. Now, the challenge for Kiffin will be getting his team off the mat and up for a game against his former team. Things have been up-and-down for transfer quarterback Sam Leavitt in Baton Rouge. The Tigers have gotten the good with the bad. Leavitt leads the SEC in completions and passing yards this season, but he also leads the conference with 12 interceptions. Leavitt is incredibly dynamic with his legs, scoring eight touchdowns on the ground and creating a dangerous running attack with Dilin Jones. We know a Kiffin offense is going to have explosive wideouts, led by the dynamic Jackson Harris on the outside. The offense has been efficient, ranking sixth in the country in Success Rate, but the turnovers and red-zone woes have killed them. When things are clicking, the offense looks great. They have just failed to come up big when needed. Defensive coordinator Blake Baker has fielded LSU's best defense in a while. This unit ranks 11th in Success Rate allowed and has been a force at creating Havoc. Defensive linemen Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross have been a force getting into the backfield and a big reason why the Tigers lead the nation in sacks. The secondary is also terrific, led by cornerbacks DJ Pickett and PJ Woodland, as well as safety Ty Benefield. The group has led the Tigers to a top-10 passing defense. LSU has allowed just eight passing touchdowns all season and has tallied 12 interceptions. With two games to go, Tennessee is on the verge of reaching the College Football Playoff for the second time in three years and is ranked in the top 10. It's Senior Night in Neyland, and old rival Kiffin is in town, so you know this crowd will be fired up. Despite the team's success, it certainly hasn't been the offense pulling the sleigh for head coach Josh Heupel. The Vols made a quarterback switch halfway through the season, benching highly-touted true freshman Faizon Brandon in favor of George MacIntyre. Both have been mixing in, with packages to use Brandon's legs. Neither quarterback has been great, and Tennessee has the fewest passing yards in the SEC this season. It lacks any explosiveness through the air. The Volunteers have been entirely relying on the running game. Running back DeSean Bishop has been terrific for the Vols all year. He has been a workhorse, leading the country with 230 carries through 10 games. Bishop has averaged over 5.0 yards per carry on all those touches, ranking top-10 in the country in yards and touchdowns. On the other side of the ball, it has been a lockdown defense leading the way for Tennessee. The Volunteers have allowed just 14.3 points per game this season, the fewest in the SEC. They rank top-10 at preventing explosives and top-five at creating Havoc. LSU might lead the country in sacks, but Tennessee ranks second, just one back. Ten players on the Vols' defense have multiple sacks this season, with Tyree Weathersby and Xavier Gilliam leading the way. The defense has been especially dominant against the pass. Tennessee has held opposing pass attacks to just 164.2 yards per game. Dejuan Lane and Ty Redmond are elite in this secondary, ashe Vols have surrendered just four passing touchdowns all season. This is a very interesting game to handicap. If you strip out all the noise and intangibles and just look at the matchup and teams on the field, you can make a case that LSU is the better team. It's more talented, ranks inside the top 11 nationally in Success Rate on offense and on defense (Tennessee ranks 40th and 34th), and most people would say it has the better coach. Nearly every trusted power rating system has LSU rated higher than Tennessee, including our Action Network Betting Power Ratings . But you can't ignore the intangibles. And something always seems to be off with LSU and with Lane Kiffin-coached teams. When it comes down to the small details, the Tigers have failed all season. They rank 103rd in the country in turnover margin, 52nd in penalties and 98th in red-zone conversion percentage. Three areas that have killed the Bayou Bengals this season. It hasn't always been pretty for Tennessee, especially on offense, but the defense has been nails. It has been absolutely dominant at home this season, allowing just 11.3 points per game at Neyland Stadium. Nobody has scored more than 20 points in Knoxville, and that includes matchups against three top-10 teams. Speaking of top-10 teams, Kiffin is now 6-19 in his career against top-10 opponents. He's 1-9 on the road against top-10 teams, with seven straight losses. He's already 0-3 against top-10 teams this season. I don't expect either offense to be overly successful in this matchup between two strong defenses. I wrote about how good Tennessee has been at home this season. But on the other side, defense often comes down to effort, motivation and give-a-damn. The Vols are certainly going to have a lot more of that. LSU is a team full of hired guns that Kiffin got out of the transfer portal for one season. Their season just ended last week. Do they care about this game? We saw the way Leavitt responded when asked about skipping the Alma Mater after last week's loss. He doesn't care about Louisiana State University. He came here to try and win a national title, and that hope is now gone. Tennessee is playing at home in Neyland Stadium, knowing how its fans feel about Kiffin and how loud that place will be, with a playoff spot and SEC Championship berth on the line. Give me the motivated team with everything still in front of it over the team of hired mercenaries with nothing to play for. Pick: Tennessee ML (Play to -110)

picks.blurb: ESPN model issues bizarre prediction for LSU-Tennessee game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended ESPN model issues bizarre prediction for LSU-Tennessee game Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads LSU and Tennessee look to be pretty evenly matched heading into Saturday's Week 12 college football action. Very evenly matched. That's according to the College Football Power Index prediction model, a computer system devised by ESPN analysts to project how teams will perform in the future. Looking over what LSU and Tennessee can put on the field , and after simulating the game 20,000 times, even they could hardly come to a conclusion. A prediction that raises eyebrows Tigers Head Coach Lane Kiffin, The LSU Tigers take on Alabama. November 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, LA, USA; at Tiger Stadium. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ESPN's model is picking the Tigers to win by exactly zero points. Yes, zero. The seemingly contradictory projection has turned some heads, particularly with Tennessee entering the matchup as the No. 9 ranked team in the country. A zero-point margin essentially suggests the model views the SEC rivals as dead even, making the Tigers' projected victory more of a technical distinction than a meaningful advantage. Tennessee has much more at stake While LSU's season, and Lane Kiffin's debut, are just about over, Tennessee has plenty on the line this weekend. The Vols' No. 9 ranking puts them inside the College Football Playoff bracket as of this week. But it's a low-enough position that they could jeopardize everything with a mistake late in the season. More: Predicting SEC football scores for Week 12's biggest games For LSU, pulling off a road victory against a nationally ranked opponent would represent at least a late-season high for Kiffin in his debut season. The numbers tell a different story Sep 12, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Tennessee Volunteers running back DeSean Bishop (18) celebrates after a touchdown run against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets in the fourth quarter at Bobby Dodd Stadium at Hyundai Field. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The prediction becomes more interesting when examining the underlying numbers. According to ESPN's matchup predictor, LSU has a 50.1 percent chance of winning, compared with Tennessee's 49.9 percent. That's essentially a statistical coin flip. However, the teams arrive with contrasting strengths. LSU averages 490.3 yards of total offense per game, ranking eighth nationally. Tennessee, meanwhile, allows just 14.3 points per game, the seventh-best scoring defense in the country. The Volunteers also rank eighth nationally in passing defense, surrendering only 164.2 yards per contest. And they're one of the best rushing teams in the country, ranking 13th with 214 yards per game. More: SEC power rankings entering college football Week 12 Can LSU pull off the upset? There is a reason ESPN's projection deserves attention. LSU's offense has demonstrated considerable firepower at times, and the Tigers have been competitive despite their 6-4 record. Three of their four losses have come by a combined six points. Still, Tennessee enters at 8-2 and has been particularly impressive at Neyland Stadium, outscoring opponents 199-68 at home this season. The takeaway? ESPN is effectively calling this matchup a toss-up, not predicting a literal scoreless-margin victory. With LSU's explosive offense facing Tennessee's formidable defense, Saturday's showdown could deliver an intriguing SEC battle.
