picks.headline: Game Preview as SMU Travels to Face No. 5 Notre Dame in Tough Road Test
picks.blurb: Game Preview as SMU Travels to Face No. 5 Notre Dame in Tough Road Test Skip to main content SI.COM MEN'S BASKETBALL WOMEN'S BASKETBALL SMU SPORTS NEWS FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2025 FOOTBALL BRACKET SI.COM MUSTANGS FB MEN'S BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM MISTANGS BB DALLAS — The SMU Mustangs (7-3, 5-3 ACC) face one of their toughest road trips of the season this weekend. The Mustangs will travel to South Bend to face the No. 5 Notre Dame Fighting Irish (9-1) Saturday night at the historic Notre Dame Stadium. The Mustangs haven’t traveled to South Bend since the late 1980s. SMU holds a 1-6 record against the Fighting Irish on the road. Notre Dame leads the all-time series 10-3 overall. SMU faces a tall task after being routed in their first ACC loss at Gerald J. Ford Stadium in over three years. The Mustangs were drilled by No. 13 Wake Forest 49-7 last week. The Demon Deacons outgained SMU 535-275 while holding the Mustangs to 209 passing yards and 69 total rushing yards. As a result, SMU's chances of heading to Charlotte for the ACC championship game and a potential shot at the College Football Playoff have grown slimmer. SMU Head Football Coach Rhett Lashlee spoke during this week's media availability on his team’s performance last week and the challenge that this week presented to bounce back. “Life’s about opportunities, we had one last week we didn't take advantage of it. We have done a good job of taking advantage of our opportunities here. We did not put our best foot forward last week,” said Lashlee during Tuesday’s media availability. “Sometimes when that happens if we were playing someone that we were expected to beat or what not. I don’t know what you gain from that, but having the opportunity to go on the road against an elite opponent we know it's going to take our very best to beat regardless of what happened last week. I like that it's a great opportunity, a great challenge, and we get to see what we are made of and how we respond to that opportunity.” Notre Dame has been a top team in college football this season. After famously being left out of the College Football Playoff last season, Head Football Coach Marcus Freeman and his team have gone to work to ensure the Fighting Irish don’t leave any boxes unchecked for a guaranteed ticket to the postseason. The Irish are 9-1 through 10 games with a staple win over the ACC leader and former No. 1 team in the country, the Miami Hurricanes, atop their season resume. Notre Dame leads the nation in the fewest yards allowed to opposing offenses. While boasting one of the nation's best offenses. Junior quarterback C.J. Carr is top 10 in passing touchdowns this season with 23, while being among the top 25 in total passing yards with 2,385 this season. Carr has been in the Heisman conversation all season in his second season as a starter. He has only been intercepted twice and sacked three times this season. He is coming off a 200-yard performance against Boston College, after throwing for a season-high 319 yards against Miami. The second-year starter has a veteran pair of wide receivers bolstering the passing attack. Senior wide receiver Jordan Faison leads the receiver room with 615 yards on 49 catches with six scores. Not far behind him is junior receiver Micah Gilbert, who has recorded 614 yards on 38 grabs with six of his own scores this season. Fellow senior Jaden Greathouse is also a reliable weapon for Carr this year, securing 25 catches for 354 yards after dealing with injury for most of last season. The multiple weapons for the home team will be a massive test on the SMU’s secondary. Pick your champion (you can change it later). We’ll email you when brackets open. After losing both star running backs to the NFL, Notre Dame’s rushing attack has been bolstered by a pair of young stars with only 11 yards separating them. Freshman running back Jonaz Walton leads the team in rushing yards with 655 yards this season, averaging 7.0 yards per carry this season with five scores. The true freshman ran for over 140 yards and a score in Notre Dame’s 41-7 win over Boston College last week. Sophomore running back Nolan James Jr. is second on the team in rushing yards with 644. The second year back has had more than 120 attempts running the football this season, with a knack for finding the end zone. James Jr. has scored 10 times so far this season, the most on the roster. SMU allowed 286 rushing yards with 6.4 yards per carry against Wake Forest last week. The Mustangs will have one of the most talented backfield duos in the country rushing at them Saturday night. Lashlee went on to describe Notre Dame’s style of play as methodical and patient, yet still able to be explosive. “The way they play allows them to be patient, methodical, and just wear on you,” said Lashlee. “Because of their talent they create explosive plays, but they are not necessarily wired where they have to. They have no problem going on 10, 12, 13 play drives and just wearing on you. So that's what you worry about over the course of the game.” SMU gears up for one of its toughest tests of the season Saturday in a game that has been circled on the calendar since the schedule was released. It doesn't matter – as long as the Irish win, they'll end up in the tournament. But drop a game over the last two weeks, and all CFP bets are off. SMU had its chance last week to all but land a spot in the ACC Championship, but one 49-7 rocking from Wake Forest later, and now it's looking to play spoiler to Notre Dame's season. Notre Dame vs SMU: Quick Hits SMU not only got blown out by Wake Forest, but that was the final home game. The Mustangs close out at Stanford. Notre Dame still has to deal with a road game at Syracuse to close things out. These two haven't played since 1989 – a 59-6 Notre Dame win. The Irish are 10-3 in the series going back to 1930. How To Watch Notre Dame vs SMU Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Notre Dame Stadium, Notre Dame, IN – Week 12 Schedule & Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – CFN Week 12 Expert Picks Why SMU Will Win SMU is still a dangerous team, even after the disaster against the Demon Deacons. The offense is terrific, with a great pace and balance that can be impossible to stop when it gets into a rhythm. Notre Dame hasn't faced too many sharp passing teams, but there was a problem against the stronger quarterbacks. BYU's Bear Bachmeier hit 65% of his passes in the 28-24 win, and Miami's Darian Mensah almost pulled the game out of the fire, throwing for 269 yards and three scores. One loss, one close call, and those were the two times the Irish allowed more than 300 total yards. SMU has one of the nation's most efficient passing games for an offense that averages 456 yards per game. Why Notre Dame Will Win How did Wake Forest destroy SMU? It came out roaring, and it was over. The Demon Deacons cranked up the pass rush against a leaky SMU line, and the three takeaways made things ugly. Yes, SMU works with a pace, but when it doesn't work, everything fizzes. But it's about the takeaways. SMU is 2-3 when turning it over multiple times, with 14 turnovers packed into those five games, and with nine turnovers in the three road games. Notre Dame is sixth in the nation in takeaways with 20. Notre Dame vs SMU Prediction, Betting Lines Yes, the Mustangs have a fun offense, and the quick-hitting style will hit the Irish defense for a few scores to throw a scare into the fan base for a half, but CJ Carr and the Notre Dame passing game are pretty good, too. Between the turnovers and lots of penalties, SMU isn't perfect. A few good drives will stall with giveaways, and even though the pass rush will get to Carr on a few third downs, the Irish will be locked in. They'll take over and pull away in the second half. Notre Dame sophomore running back Nolan James Jr. has also racked up over 600 rushing yards, and junior halfback Aneyas Williams has made significant contributions from the backfield as well. It's Notre Dame's defensive unit that has made the Irish one of the best teams in the nation — ranking 10th nationally in EPA per Pass allowed and 16th in Pass Success Rate allowed. The question will be whether that Irish defense can slow down the Kevin Jennings-led SMU squad. Notre Dame's spectacular defensive unit will face an elite Mustang offense in a matchup that pits two contrasting styles of play against each other. While SMU's aforementioned -6 turnover margin is concerning on the surface, it's even more so when you consider Notre Dame's impressive +16 turnover margin, with the Irish rarely giving away extra possessions. Jennings cannot afford to commit turnovers early in Saturday night's matchup, in what could be a very long night under center against Notre Dame's elite defense. I feel confident backing Freeman's Fighting Irish to cover both the 20.5-point full-game spread and an alternate 9.5 first-half spread at -135. This should be a one-sided affair. Pick: Notre Dame -20.5 , Notre Dame 1H alt -9.5 (-135)

picks.blurb: Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame vs SMU Game Predictions (Angela Driskell, Irish Breakdown) Bryan Driskell · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 2:00 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Notre Dame will look to build its College Football Playoff resume when it takes on the 7-3 SMU Mustangs. The Irish fell to 6th in the playoff rankings on Tuesday despite blowing out Boston College by a 41-7 score last weekend. Notre Dame doesn't have a ranked opponent left on the schedule, but the Mustangs will help improve the overall strength of schedule, should the Irish earn a win. Notre Dame makes the playoff if they win out, but a dominant win would be even more helpful. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET Networ k: NBC/Peacock Here are our staff predictions for the game: Prediction : Notre Dame 38, SMU 17 Some of the magnitude of this game was diminished when SMU lost to Wake Forest last weekend in a blowout (49-7). SMU is a much better football team than it showed against the Demon Deacons, and that game reminded me a lot of Notre Dame's loss to Miami in 2017. It was one of those games that just got away from them early, but make no mistake, SMU is a dangerous football team. Notre Dame will need to play at a high level, because I expect SMU to come out looking to make an early statement and bounce back from their bad loss last weekend. The key for Notre Dame will be coming out early and jumping all over the Mustangs. They will need to quickly take away SMU's confidence and not let their potent offense get into any kind of rhythm. That will require the defense to be turned loose and be allowed to attack quarterback Kevin Jennings . If they are allowed to do that, and if the DL handles business, they will force Jennings to make mistakes, and that's how Notre Dame rolls in this game. My prediction is based on SMU being able to make some plays early due to their impressive talent at wide receiver and the fact Jennings is a dangerous player. I expect the Irish defense to quickly get up to speed and slow SMU down over the final two quarters. On the other side of the ball, Notre Dame will look to establish the run game early and get Nolan James Jr . and Jonaz Walton to get going. They will look to soften the Mustangs up and that's when CJ Carr should get rolling and pick the Mustangs apart. If the offensive line handles business the Notre Dame offense should have a big day and the Irish should roll. If Carr gets going early the offense could be extremely difficult to stop in this matchup. Prediction : Notre Dame 41, SMU 13 This is the final of three major tests for the 6th ranked Notre Dame Fighting Irish. SMU is coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest at home during their own Senior Day matchup, but don't let that fool you, this is still a talented team making the trip up north. But like a lot of their opponents for the 2026 season, this matchup is more about Notre Dame living up to its potential than it is about facing an opponent that's superior. As it was said best in Wednesday's show, Marcus Freeman needs to know 'what time it is' in college football. SMU is a quality opponent, but not good enough that simply winning the game will boost their resume all on its own. I expect the Fighting Irish offense to come out firing early. Quarterback CJ Carr will hit some big plays early. The biggest question, will Notre Dame keep their foot on the gas after jumping out to an early lead? I think they answer that to a degree, but Freeman needs to learn from the lessons he's experienced in the previous two seasons. I have the Irish winning by 28 on Senior Day. I'm picking Notre Dame to win convincingly against SMU, but this game is about more than simply adding another win to the schedule. With the College Football Playoff committee evaluating every result, the Irish need to make a statement and show that they belong among the nation's elite. Notre Dame cannot afford to play down to its competition or let SMU hang around into the second half. This is an opportunity to dominate on both sides of the football, establish the running game, stretch the field offensively, and demonstrate the kind of physical superiority that separates playoff contenders from everyone else. The Irish need to take care of business, but they also need to make it look impressive. SMU has enough offensive talent, particularly with quarterback Kevin Jennings , to make things interesting if Notre Dame allows it. However, coming off a 49-7 loss to Wake Forest, the Mustangs are vulnerable, and Notre Dame needs to take full advantage. I want to see the Irish defense create turnovers, get after Jennings, and keep SMU from finding any offensive rhythm. More importantly, Notre Dame needs to keep its foot on the gas rather than become conservative with a comfortable lead. The committee won't just see another win but it will see how the Irish perform against an opponent they are expected to handle. This is a chance to deliver a dominant performance, build momentum, and send a message that Notre Dame is a legitimate national championship contender. Prediction : Notre Dame 52, SMU 13 Before last weekend, I was going to pick a closer game (something like 38-24), but a combination of both the SMU blowout loss to Wake Forest and Notre Dame's dominant win over Boston College made me reconsider. First, I was pleased that the Irish played the attacking style of defense against Boston College that we saw for the second half of 2025, early in 2026, and then again against Miami. I don't think SMU's offensive line can hold up against the Irish front-seven when they play aggressively. The Mustangs gave up three sacks and six tackles for loss to Wake Forest, and rank 96th in the country in sacks allowed in road games this season. Getting SMU behind the sticks is going to put the onus on Kevin Jennings to make plays. He is really talented, but has a penchant for putting the ball in danger and making a few of those "what is he doing" kind of plays per game. There's a reason that SMU ranks 118th in the country in turnover margin at -6, and Notre Dame ranks 2nd at +16. Also, whether its due to corruption, malice, or just plain incompetence, there are no guarantees for Notre Dame when it comes to the CFP Committee. Marcus Freeman knows that it's not enough to just win these final two games - the Irish need to be dominant if they want to secure a home playoff game. With Wake Forest having such a big win last weekend over SMU - in Dallas no less - I think that will force Freeman and the Irish to keep the pedal down more than would be typical on a Senior Day when the staff typically tries to get all seniors a couple snaps once the game is in hand. Notre Dame's offense should not have much trouble moving the ball against a Mustangs defense that was blitzed by the two best offenses it faced (giving up 488.5 YPG against ranked opponents), and I think the Irish send a message on the scoreboard. Prediction : Notre Dame 35, SMU 10 SMU is a rising program, no question, which was why I was definitely surprised to tune into the game in the second half on Saturday to see such a lopsided score against Wake Forest. The Demon Deacons hammered SMU, leaving them off the scoreboard in the first half and quickly lighting up the scoreboard. While the Mustangs can certainly compete with anybody and Saturday's score was definitely out of character with how their season has gone, I don't think Notre Dame will have much trouble with them, provided they get off to a good start and play disciplined football. It really feels like Mike Denbrock has found his groove, with a great mix of run-and-pass with CJ Carr and Notre Dame's three-headed monster in the backfield: Jonaz Walton , Nolan James Jr. and Aneyas Williams . Give me the Irish.

away.blurb: SMU might be having an up-and-down season, but that doesn’t mean the Mustangs' offense isn’t one to be reckoned with. That’s one reason Notre Dame is so excited about the possibility of getting safety Brauntae Johnson back this week. It’s also why the news that defensive tackle Francis Brewu is officially off the availability report is big: it means he’ll be available to play Saturday night. Brewu, who has missed the last two games due to injury, has been an impact player since arriving in South Bend via the transfer portal from Pittsburgh. The 6-foot-1, 285-pound junior was removed from Thursday’s availability update after being listed as questionable Monday. He suffered the knee injury on October 31 against Navy, leaving that game after just a handful of snaps. Another defensive lineman for Notre Dame also has a chance to make his season debut. Sophomore Christopher Burgess Jr. was removed from Thursday’s availability report after previously being listed as out with a left tibia injury suffered before preseason camp. Like Brauntae Johnson, there’s a question about whether Burgess will actually play, given how long he’s been out. When defensive coordinator Chris Ash talked about Johnson earlier this week , he made it clear that the missed time could mean the safety won’t make the SMU game and would instead be ready later in the season. It’s a safe assumption that Burgess could face a similar challenge. Johnson, sophomore left tackle Will Black (concussion) and sixth-year defensive lineman Jason Onye (right knee) all remain questionable. Onye is another player who has missed significant time this year , and the fact that there’s even a chance he could get on the field against SMU is a good sign, especially with the College Football Playoff kicking off next month and the Irish still fighting for a berth. away.headline: Notre Dame football's top run-stuffer set to return vs. SMU
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND — Junior defensive tackle Francis Brewu is to set to return for Notre Dame football this week against Southern Methodist after missing nearly three full games with a left knee injury. The 6-foot-1, 285-pound Pittsburgh transfer had been listed as questionable on the official injury report since going down seven snaps into the Navy game on Oct. 31 in Foxborough, MA. Fellow defensive tackle Jason Onye, injured five snaps into the Navy game, remains questionable with a right knee injury as of Thursday’s late-week availability update. Return to play: Notre Dame football must work Brauntae Johnson back into game shape Partridge recruited Brewu to Pitt out of Westerville, OH before spending the 2024-25 seasons with the Indianapolis Colts. The reunion has been good for both parties. “We made sure and pointed it out (in film study),” Partridge said of Brewu’s advanced technique against Navy. “That's just an example of how he's playing the game right now. I’m proud of him. I’m happy for him.” This article originally appeared on South Bend Tribune: Notre Dame football's top run-stuffer set to return vs. SMU “(Brewu) has played really, really well,” defensive line coach Charlie Partridge said in early November. “I'm proud of his growth. He's had a lot to learn since he's been here. It's a completely different style of defense than Pittsburgh plays, and it was a challenge for him early. “ Brewu averaged 24 defensive snaps through the first seven games, peaking at 35 snaps in the Oct. 17 loss at BYU. His 84.3 overall defensive grade, per Pro Football Focus, is tied for eighth among FBS defensive tackles with at least 175 snaps this season. His 84.5 grade as a run stuffer is seventh. Oregon transfer Tionne Gray (70.1) is tied for 139th overall at defensive tackle, while Armel Mukam (69.1) is tied for 161st. “Because I've known him so long, I was probably harder on him than some of the other guys,” Partridge said. “But I was that way because I want him to be the best version of himself. And to his credit, he weathered that storm and was playing really good football (before the injury).” Brewu averaged 37 defensive snaps across 13 games in 2025 at Pitt with a high of 61 in Week 3 at West Virginia. His overall PFF grade was 78.4, tying him for 17th among the 147 defensive tackles with at least 450 games snaps last year. “He's rushing the passer well, he's playing the run well,” Partridge said. “There was a play against Navy where it was beautiful. He played the cut (block) with two hands, he cleared the cut, and he leapt off the ground to tackle the guy from behind. Not many people are going to put that on their bingo card to say, ‘I'm going to put this on Instagram.’“ Brewu is tied for third on the team with two sacks, and he counts three tackles for loss among his 16 total tackles. Mike Berardino covers Notre Dame football for the South Bend Tribune and NDInsider.com. Follow him on social media @MikeBerardino.

Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. EST on SEC Network. Missouri is favored by 5.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -210. The total is set at 48.5 points. Here's my Kentucky vs. Missouri prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 21, 2026. Kentucky vs. Missouri Pick: Kentucky +5.5 (-110) My Missouri vs. Kentucky best bet is on the Wildcats to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Kentucky vs Missouri Odds Kentucky vs Missouri point spread : Missouri -5.5 (-110), Kentucky +5.5 (-110) Kentucky vs Missouri over/under : 48.5 (-110o / -110u) Kentucky vs Missouri moneyline : Kentucky +172, Missouri -210 Kentucky heads to Columbia at 7-3 following consecutive losses to Tennessee and Florida , and while the Wildcats have struggled offensively over the last two weeks, I'm willing to buy low on Will Stein's team against a Missouri offense that hasn't consistently demonstrated the ability to create separation. The Cats were held to just six points against the Vols before losing 21-14 to Florida, and the offensive line struggled badly in both matchups. Against the Gators, Kentucky generated only 61 rushing yards on 27 carries, averaging 2.3 yards per carry. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has thrown for 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns, and just two interceptions while completing nearly 69% of his passes. That's an encouraging season-long profile. Wide receiver Kenny Darby has recorded 601 receiving yards, while running back CJ Baxter has rushed for 562 yards and eight scores. Baxter's availability remains worth monitoring after earlier injury reports, but Kentucky has shown considerably more offensive consistency than its last two box scores suggest. The Wildcats rank 21st nationally in Success Rate at 48.3% and 28th in Finishing Drives, generating 4.02 points per scoring opportunity. They also rarely turn the ball over, and that ball security is particularly important against a Missouri defense capable of generating disruption and creating short fields. Pass protection remains a concern, especially after the performance against Florida. But Minchey's ability to consistently complete underneath passes gives the Wildcats an opportunity to sustain possessions. If the Cats can control the clock and protect the ball, I expect them to keep this game within one score throughout the evening. Missouri enters Saturday at 6-4 after an ugly 48-21 loss to Georgia , and while the Tigers have more than enough offensive talent to win this matchup, I'm having a hard time trusting them to cover nearly a full touchdown. Quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 2,379 yards, 21 touchdowns, and just three picks. Wide receiver Cayden Lee leads Missouri with 879 receiving yards, while running back Jamal Roberts has rushed for 1,133 yards and nine scores. Those are impressive individual numbers, but the underlying efficiency profile raises some concerns. The Tigers rank 103rd nationally in offensive Success Rate at just 40.7% while generating only 3.23 points per scoring opportunity (99th in Finishing Drives). As you can see, serious regression has begun. Missouri also converts just 38.2% of its third downs, ranking 95th nationally. The offensive line has done an excellent job limiting disruption, allowing Havoc on just 2.1% of snaps in the model's metric. However, that protection hasn't translated into the down-to-down efficiency necessary to sustain scoring drives. Missouri's defense has been considerably more reliable, allowing a 38.7% Success Rate (29th nationally) while generating Havoc on 5.2% of snaps (36th). The offense has been playing with fire most of the season. Simmons' numbers look a lot prettier than they should, and I wouldn't be surprised to see the free fall continue over the next couple of weeks. Missouri opened as a 6.5-point favorite before getting bet down toward MIZ -5.5, and I'm willing to take the points with Kentucky. The biggest reason is the discrepancy in offensive efficiency. The Finishing Drives matchup is particularly important, as the Wildcats should be able to stay within the number if the Tigers are forced to settle for field goals. Both teams are coming off consecutive losses, and I'm not interested in pretending either has a significant motivational advantage. However, Kentucky's recent results have created a chance to buy low on a team whose season-long efficiency remains respectable. My biggest concern is the Wildcats' third-down defense, which allows opponents to convert 52.3% of their attempts, ranking near the bottom nationally. That's a legitimate advantage for Simmons and Missouri's passing attack. However, given the Tigers' red-zone issues, I expect them to struggle to turn those opportunities into touchdowns. I think this will be an ugly game all around, with the Cats staying within striking distance. Pick: Kentucky +5.5 (-110)

picks.headline: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back?
picks.blurb: Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games MLB trade targets Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended Story by Wildcats Wire Missouri Defense Preview: Can Kentucky's offense bounce back? Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Thu, November 19, 2026 at 1:25 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels to CoMo for the final road game of the season against the Missouri Tigers. The Wildcats offense desperately needs to respond after scoring just 20 points in the last two weeks which has led to back-to-back losses. Missouri is a well coached, good all around football team and the defense has been consistent this season. However, the Tigers had their worst defensive performance of the season on the road last week against Georgia. Both teams are coming off back-to-back losses, Kentucky has scored just 20 points on offense in the past two weeks. Conversely, the Missouri defense has allowed 72 points over the last two weeks, albeit to Georgia and Texas. Kentucky has to find some of the offensive success they had before the bye week if they want to finish the season on a strong note. A win at Missouri would give the Wildcats six wins in SEC play, which has only happened once in program history and that was in the 1977 season. I fully expect a motivated performance from both teams to try and put an end to their respective two-game losing streaks. Kentucky's offensive line was named a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award and have since had to of their worst performances of the season. Last week against Florida was the worst the offensive line has looked all season, so you can almost guarantee they will respond the right way in this game. Quiet frankly, they have to because if the offensive line plays like they did against the Gators they will be in danger of a winless month of November. Missouri's defense has playmakers at every level, but they will allow teams to move the football. Among SEC teams, the Tigers rank 10th in success rate allowed, 7th in pass success rate allowed and 12th in rush success rate allowed. Missouri also ranks 8th in the SEC in EPA/play allowed, 7th in EPA/pass allowed and 12th in EPA/rush allowed. The Tigers have also allowed explosive plays this season, as they rank 14th in the conference in explosive play rate allowed. This will be a difficult matchup for Kentucky, but it starts by winning the line of scrimmage and getting the run game going. The Wildcats averaged just two yards per carry against Florida and had just 61 rushing yards. They will lose this game if they can not turn that around, but the Missouri run defense has struggled at times this season. Kentucky has to stay ahead of the chains and that starts with the run game on early downs, which is something they had been good at all season. We mentioned the Tigers have playmakers at every level of the defense, and that starts up front with edge defender Daeden Hopkins. Hopkins leads the team in sacks (7) and tackles for loss (7.5). Linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez leads the middle of the defense, Rodriguez is a tackling machine with a team-leading 107 tackles on the season; he also has seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks on the year. The secondary is led by safety Santana Banner, Banner has 84 tackles on the season, 6 pass breakups and 2.5 tackles for loss. Kentucky has to account for these three players, as they are the strength of this Missouri defense at every level. Hopkins, Rodriguez and Banner have each forced two fumbles this season as well. They have consistently made big time plays for the Tigers all season long. Kentucky has to find ways to exploit this defense and avoid letting these three players make game changing plays. In a lot of ways, this matchup is about Kentucky after scoring just 20 points in the last eight quarters. The offense just is not playing well, and what happened on the line of scrimmage against Florida was alarming. Kentucky has to get the big blue wall back to playing like semifinalists for the Joe Moore Award. This offense lacks explosive plays and yards after contact ability, so they will continue to struggle if the offensive line can't get back to playing at a high level. Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 21, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Can the Cats get back on track? Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. Missouri 2026 Results W 54-14 vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff W 38-21 vs. Kansas W 27-17 vs. Troy L 31-24 at Mississippi State W 45-17 vs. Florida W 27-6 vs. Texas A&M L 31-3 at Ole Miss W 34-10 at Arkansas L 34-20 vs. Texas L 48-21 at Georgia Players to Know QB Austin Simmons: He won the job over Matt Zollers in the spring and opened the season 17 of 19 for 252 yards and four touchdowns. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. It won’t be pretty, but the Cats grind out a road win and stay alive for a 10-win season. Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.headline: How No. 16 Kentucky football and Missouri match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.8% completions, 2,160 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had a challenging game in UK’s 21-14 upset loss to visiting Florida last week. The 6-foot-2, 211-pound product of Hendersonville, Tennessee, completed only 15 of 26 passes for 181 yards with one touchdown. In going 0-2 since returning from an Oct. 31 open week, Kentucky has allowed too much pressure on its QB. Minchey has been sacked six times and hurried 10 times total in losses to Tennessee and Florida. • Missouri’s Austin Simmons (62.3% completions, 2,379 yards, 21 touchdowns vs. three interceptions) has thrown for seven combined touchdowns in Mizzou’s past three games. A 6-4, 220-pound product of Miami, Simmons has already started a game vs. UK. Playing last season for Ole Miss, Simmons made his first career road start at Kroger Field. The QB threw two early picks as Ole Miss fell behind 10-0. Simmons steadied, however, and threw for 235 yards and ran for 44 yards and a TD as the Rebels rallied to beat Kentucky 30-23. Advantage : Missouri Running backs • UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (562 yards, 5.3 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the loss vs. Florida but had a hard time on the ground vs. the Gators. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, rushed 8 times for 21 yards vs. his home-state school. Since missing the Oklahoma game due to injury, Baxter has subsequently carried 20 times for 78 yards in the three games. Third-year player Jason Patterson (495 yards, 6 yards a carry, three TDs) had 22 yards on five rushes vs. Florida and caught a pass for nine yards. • Missouri’s Jamal Roberts (1,133 yards, 5 yards a carry, nine touchdowns) is second in the SEC in rushing. A 6-foot, 216-pound St. Louis product, Roberts has run for 100 yards or more in five games this season, and has gone above 200 yards rushing in a game twice. Ahmad Hardy led the SEC in rushing in 2025, running for 1,649 yards and 16 touchdowns. However, the 5-10, 210-pound product of Oma, Mississippi, missed the first seven games this season as he recovered from being shot in the left leg May 10 while attending an outdoor concert in Laurel, Mississippi. Since returning three games ago, Hardy has carried 10 times for 41 yards. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (49 catches, 601 yards, three touchdowns) needs two catches and 29 receiving yards to shatter Barion Brown’s UK freshman marks (50 receptions, 628 receiving yards in 2022) for most catches and receiving yards in a season. Second-year player DJ Miller (26, 324, 1) caught four passes for 80 yards vs. Florida but also had a costly drop on UK’s final offensive possession of the game. • Missouri’s Cayden Lee is second in the SEC in receptions and first in the conference in receiving yards (879). A transfer from Ole Miss, the 5-11, 180-pound fourth-year player has caught at least five passes in every Mizzou game in 2026 other than last week’s 48-21 loss at No. 1 Georgia, when he was held to three receptions for 44 yards. Lee caught one pass for eight yards for Ole Miss in its win at Kentucky last season. Sophomore Donovan Olugbode is also having a big year for Missouri. The 6-2, 210-pound Chicago product has made 47 catches for 691 yards and eight touchdowns. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez is tied for fifth in the FBS in receptions by a tight end with 50. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School has turned those team-high 50 receptions into 467 receiving yards and three touchdowns. A model of consistency, Rodriguez has caught either five or six passes in each of UK’s past six games. • Missouri’s Brett Norfleet has 14 catches for 120 yards and two TDs. The 6-6, 255-pound fourth-year player caught one pass for seven yards in last week’s loss to Georgia. Jude James has averaged 10 yards a catch on his seven receptions. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • In the losses to Tennessee and Florida the past two weeks, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has seemed to struggle in pass protection. Of the 6-8, 329-pound Madison Central product, Will Stein said “We all know, I know, (I) think everybody on our team knows (Wood’s) talent level is as good as you’re going to find in the country. It’s just consistency at that position.” • Missouri left tackle Cayden Green is the pillar of a Tigers offensive front that has surrendered the fewest QB sacks (nine) in the SEC. After starting five times for Oklahoma in 2023, Green transferred to Mizzou and started all 13 games in 2024 at left guard. Since switching to left tackle prior to the 2025 season, the 6-5, 324-pound Green has become a standout. So far in 2026, he has not allowed a sack or quarterback hit. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (36 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) had a streak of three straight games with at least one sack snapped vs. Florida. Tackle Tavion Gadson (33 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) also made four stops against the Gators. Gadson has now gone three games without a sack. • Missouri defensive end Daeden Hopkins is fourth in the SEC with seven sacks. The 6-6, 250-pound second-year player has also been credited with 11 quarterback hurries. A transfer from Miami, second-year tackle Donta Simpson has emerged as a disruptor for Eli Drinkwitz and Co. The 6-4, 300-pound Simpson has six QB sacks, 7.5 tackles for loss and eight QB hurries. Advantage : Even • Even though Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey (13 tackles) and WLB Bo Barnes (nine stops) were UK’s two leading tacklers vs. Florida, the prevailing thought was that UF’s ample success with the QB run game owed, in some part, to the Wildcats’ linebackers not fitting the run properly. “There were some big, big missed tackles in the game that sprung explosive runs by their quarterback,” Will Stein said. “That goes back to us not executing the fundamentals and technique of our position.” • Missouri WLB Nicholas Rodriguez leads the SEC in tackles with 107. The 6-foot, 225-pound Miami product has made at least 11 tackles in eight of Mizzou’s 10 games to date. MLB Robert Woodyard Jr ., a transfer from Auburn, is 22nd in the SEC with 64 tackles and has forced two fumbles and picked off a pass. Defensive backs • Kentucky safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant are tied for second in the SEC in interceptions with four apiece. However, neither has a pick in either of UK’s past two games, the losses at Tennessee and to Florida. Castell, a 6-2, 211-pound product of Orlando, is ninth in the SEC with 76 tackles. Bryant, a 6-foot, 196-pound Lexington native, is 12th in the SEC with 74 stops. • Missouri cornerbacks Sione Laulea and Chris Graves Jr. are tied for second in the SEC with 10 passes successfully defended. Strong safety Santana Banner has recovered two fumbles and broken up six passes. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. For the second time this season, UK switched punters vs. Florida. Craig has been better from outside 50 yards (5 of 7, 71.4%) than from inside 50 yards (10 of 17, 58.8%). Punter Brunno Reus is averaging 44.47 yards a kick and has stopped 18 of 47 punts inside the opponent’s 20-yard line. Punt returner DaMarion Fowlkes averaged 10 yards a return and had a 68-yard TD vs. Troy. As a kickoff returner, Fowlkes is averaging 24.8 yards on 12 returns. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Stanford vs California Prediction 11/21/2026 Today's College Football Picks Chris Ruffolo Stanford Cardinal California Golden Bears Over 55.5 (-110) Under 55.5 (-110) California Memorial Stadium, Berkeley, CA Saturday, November 21, 2026 Ron Romanelli Big Al McMordie See the full rankings: Best College Football Handicappers Stanford Cardinal vs Cal Golden Bears Prediction I'm laying the points with Stanford against Cal in the Big Game. I know rivalry games can make records look meaningless, and the Golden Bears would love nothing more than to keep their neighbors out of a bowl game. But at some point, I have to back the team that's actually moving in the right direction. Stanford has won three of its last four, while Cal has lost four straight and looks completely out of answers under Tosh Lupoi. The Cardinal can become bowl eligible for the first time since 2018, and I think they're playing with the urgency to make that happen. What's changed for Stanford is that the offense finally has something it can lean on. Micah Ford has rushed for at least 145 yards in three of the last four games, and he's averaging 137.5 rushing yards since the win over Elon. He just ran for 149 yards and three touchdowns in a 40-22 victory at Virginia Tech. That's a big deal against a Cal defense allowing 186.2 rushing yards per game. Stanford hasn't been a great rushing team over the entire season, but Ford's recent form gives the Cardinal a way to control possessions instead of asking Davis Warren to do everything. Warren has quietly done a nice job protecting the football. He's thrown for 2,406 yards with 14 touchdowns and only three interceptions, despite ranking among the national leaders in pass attempts. Stanford is still converting just 31.7 percent of its third downs, so it's not as though every offensive problem has disappeared. But when you can get the running game going and avoid handing the opponent short fields, you give yourself a much better chance to win close games. That's been missing from this program for a while. Cal's offense is the bigger concern for me. The Bears are scoring just 20.4 points per game and averaging only 78.7 rushing yards. That's an awful lot of pressure on Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, who's thrown 11 touchdowns against eight interceptions. Chase Hendricks has been productive with 65 catches, but defenses don't have to respect the run nearly enough. Cal managed seven points at Virginia last week, and that loss followed defeats to Wake Forest , SMU and NC State. Those four losses have come by at least three touchdowns apiece. That's not a team that's simply catching a few unlucky breaks. I won't pretend Stanford is some defensive powerhouse. The Cardinal allow 35.8 points and nearly 449 yards per game, numbers that give Cal a legitimate opportunity to move the ball. But Stanford forced three turnovers against Virginia Tech, with Charlie Eckhardt recording two interceptions and a forced fumble. That was the Cardinal's first road win since 2024, snapping a 15-game skid away from home. The defense doesn't suddenly become great because of one afternoon, but there are signs of improvement when the offense gives it a chance. The travel angle is another reason I don't mind the road favorite here. Stanford has been crushed on several cross-country trips since joining the ACC, but going from Palo Alto to Berkeley is hardly the same situation. Cal also returns home after three straight road games, so maybe getting back to its own building helps. They haven't played in Berkeley since October 17, so there's some uncertainty there. The Bears have won the last two Big Games played in Berkeley, and that matters in a rivalry. Stanford, though, took back the Axe with a 31-10 win last season. Now there's a bowl bid waiting on the other side of another rivalry victory, while Cal is already eliminated from postseason consideration. Chris Ruffolo's Pick: Stanford -2.5 Need More? The TCU Horned Frogs will face one of their toughest challenges of the season Saturday when they host No. 2 Utah at Amon G. Carter Stadium. The Frogs are coming off a 20-10 victory over Kansas State , while the Utes enter the matchup looking to keep their undefeated season alive. Utah is 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big 12 play. Saturday's matchup will mark the highest-ranked opponent to visit Amon G. Carter Stadium since No. 2 Texas in 1970. It also marks TCU's final home game of the season before the Frogs travel to face Texas Tech on Thanksgiving Day. With a win, TCU would secure bowl eligibility and pull off one of the biggest upsets of the college football season. When TCU has the ball Quarterback Jaden Craig will be a key factor in TCU's ability to keep up with Utah's offense. Craig has thrown for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season. He is coming off a 225-yard performance against Kansas State, where he also threw a touchdown pass. The Horned Frogs will need to find ways to create offensive opportunities without relying entirely on Craig's arm. Establishing the run game and finding success on early downs will be important against a Utah defense that has helped the Utes remain undefeated. Craig has also been dealing with an ankle injury that has limited his mobility. However, head coach Sonny Dykes said during Tuesday's midweek news conference that Craig is showing improvement and is expected to play Saturday. "I would expect him to play. He was a lot better today than he was yesterday. I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday," Dykes said Tuesday. TCU will need to sustain drives, limit mistakes and take advantage of its scoring opportunities if it hopes to pull off the upset. The Frogs showed they can do that with their 20-10 victory over Kansas State. When Kansas State has the ball Undefeated Utah has been one of the strongest teams in the Big 12 this season and is looking to secure a spot in the conference championship game. The Utes will be one of TCU's toughest defensive challenges yet. The Frogs will need to limit Utah's scoring opportunities and find ways to slow down its offense if they hope to keep the game competitive. Quarterback Devon Dampier has completed 66.5% of his passes for 2,257 yards, 22 touchdowns and eight interceptions this season. His ability to make plays through the air will put pressure on TCU's secondary. TCU's defense will need to create pressure, limit big plays and force Utah into difficult third-down situations. If the Frogs cannot slow down Dampier and the Utes' offense, it could be a long night for the defense. This will be one of the toughest games of the season for the Horned Frogs. TCU is coming off a big win over Kansas State and will be hungry to prove it can compete with one of the best teams in the country. While I expect the Frogs to put up a fight, they have struggled to perform consistently under pressure this season. Utah has remained undefeated for a reason, and its strength on both sides of the ball will make this a difficult matchup for TCU. I expect the Horned Frogs to compete early, but Utah's consistency will ultimately be too much to overcome. Schobel got his most extensive action of his career in the win over the Wildcats, mostly on designed quarterback runs, but will now be tasked to lead the Horned Frogs against the highest-ranked opponent to play in the Carter since No. 2 Texas in 1970. home.headline: What's TCU quarterback's status for the showdown with No. 2 Utah?
home.blurb: TCU football is expecting senior quarterback Jaden Craig to be available against No. 2 Utah on Saturday. While Craig will be available on Saturday, it appears he still not be 100% and that means the Horned Frogs could rely on sophomore quarterback Adam Schobel. Schobel played about half a dozen snaps against the Wildcats, rushing for three yards on three carries. “I love Adam; we came in at the same time. He was a freshman when I transferred in,” Pimpton said. “So I have a great relationship with Adam. I’m pretty sure Jay’s going to tough it and play. He’s gonna go out there and do his thing regardless. Whoever goes out there, we will ride behind him no matter what goes on.” Craig was hobbled during TCU’s 20-10 win over Kansas State last Saturday with a lower body injury, but is expected to be a full-go when the Horned Frogs (5-5, 3-4 Big 12) host the Utes (10-0, 7-0) at 8 p.m. on Fox . “I would expect him to play,” TCU head coach Sonny Dykes said Tuesday. “He was a lot better today than he was yesterday, and so I would anticipate him being able to practice tomorrow and play on Saturday. That would be my guess.” If Schobel has to play more against Utah, Dykes doesn’t anticipate the offense needing to change much to fit his skillset. “I think Adam’s a little more mobile than Jaden, and so that would change, but not really,” Dykes said. “The playbook wouldn’t change much. Adam’s been repping our offense all fall camp and all season. So he can go in and execute what we need if we needed him to.” If Schobel gets a bigger role against the Utes, he’ll have the full support of his teammates, like senior tight end Ka’Morreun Pimpton. home.blurb: TCU QB Adam Schobel expected to start over doubtful Jaden Craig vs. Utah - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF TCU QB Adam Schobel expected to start over doubtful Jaden Craig vs. Utah The TCU Horned Frogs face a massive hurdle ahead of Saturday's showdown against the No. 2 Utah Utes. Starting quarterback Jaden Craig landed on Friday night's Big 12 availability report as doubtful, putting sophomore backup Adam Schobel in line to make his first career start, per ESPN's Pete Thamel. TCU listed Craig as probable earlier in the week before downgrading him Friday night. Losing Craig deals a major blow to a 5-5 Horned Frogs offense chasing bowl eligibility against an undefeated 10-0 Utah squad. The Harvard transfer ranks third in the Big 12 with 266.4 passing yards per game, completing 223 of 344 throws for 2,664 yards, 13 touchdowns and seven interceptions while adding four rushing scores. Against Kansas State last Saturday, Craig went 20-for-34 for 225 yards and a touchdown without throwing a pick. Now, the spotlight shifts to Schobel. The 6-foot-5 former four-star recruit from Columbus, Texas, has seen limited action across three appearances this season. He threw one incomplete pass against the Grambling Tigers in September and logged four carries for 11 yards, including three rushes for three yards against Kansas State. TCU's injury woes extend beyond the quarterback room. The Horned Frogs also ruled out running back G'Ivori Graham and linebacker Keylan Abrams for Saturday's contest in Fort Worth, though defensive tackles Markis Deal and Ansel Din-Mbuh alongside edge rusher Cheta Ofili remain probable. Meanwhile, Utah ruled out safety Marcus Wimberly and listed long snapper Logan Castor as questionable. Throwing a first-time starter against the Big 12's top team is no easy task, but Schobel gets his shot to shock college football under the Fort Worth lights.
